The diffusion of AI into mental health care is often framed in highly optimistic terms: technologies that reduce stigma, democratize access, and provide affordable, always-on support (M & N, 2025;Sivasubramanian Balasubramanian, 2023). From meditation applications and emotion-tracking wearables to conversational agents offering cognitive-behavioral interventions, AI is marketed as an efficient and reliable partner in the pursuit of wellbeing (Balcombe, 2023).Beneath this enthusiasm lies a paradox. On one hand, AI enables cognitive offloading: the use of external aids to reduce mental effort and conserve resources for more meaningful activities (Grinschgl & Neubauer, 2022;Risko & Gilbert, 2016). This process can support adaptive coping, helping individuals regulate stress and sustain mental health. On the other hand, the same tools may create cognitive overload: an erosion of introspection, over-reliance on algorithmic feedback, and anxiety induced by hyper-monitoring and optimization (Grinschgl et al., 2021;Skulmowski, 2023). The question is not whether AI is good or bad for mental health but how it is reshaping the very architecture of coping (Gerlich, 2025). This article examines the psychology of this paradox. First, it places copings in mainstream psychological theory. Then it considers the promise of AI to lighten burdens through cognitive offloading. Next, it considers the risks of cognitive overload and theoretical insights that illuminate this conflict. Through practic

hot.title: A Comparison of Responses from Human Therapists and Large Language Model–Based Chatbots to Assess Therapeutic Communication: Mixed Methods Study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consumers are increasingly using large language model-based chatbots to seek mental health advice or intervention due to ease of access and limited availability of mental health professionals. However, their suitability and safety for mental health applications remain underexplored, particularly in comparison to professional therapeutic practices. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how general-purpose chatbots respond to mental health scenarios and compare their responses to those provided by licensed therapists. Specifically, we sought to identify chatbots' strengths and limitations, as well as the ethical and practical considerations necessary for their use in mental health care. METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study to compare responses from chatbots and licensed therapists to scripted mental health scenarios. We created 2 fictional scenarios and prompted 3 chatbots to create 6 interaction logs. We recruited 17 therapists and conducted study sessions that consisted of 3 activities. First, therapists responded to the 2 scenarios using a Qualtrics form. Second, therapists went through the 6 interaction logs using a think-aloud procedure to highlight their thoughts about the chatbots' responses. Finally, we conducted a semistructured interview to explore subjective opinions on the use of chatbots for supporting mental health. The study sessions were analyzed using thematic analysis. The interaction logs from chatbot and therapist responses were coded using the Multitheoretical List of Therapeutic Interventions codes and then compared to each other. RESULTS: We identified 7 themes describing the strengths and limitations of the chatbots as compared to therapists. These include elements of good therapy in chatbot responses, conversational style of c

hot.title: Strategic human resource management in the digital economy era: an empirical study of challenges and opportunities among MSMEs and startups in Indonesia
hot.abstract: This study investigates the impact of digital Human Resource Management (HRM) strategies on workforce productivity and organizational performance within Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and startups in Indonesia. Anchored in the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the research conceptualizes digital HRM as a strategic asset that enhances organizational performance by enabling firms to develop, deploy, and reconfigure human capital capabilities in response to digital transformation. The conceptual model includes five constructs: Digital Technology Adoption in HRM, Digital Training and Development, Work Flexibility and Hybrid Management, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention, and Utilization of HR Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Data were collected through structured questionnaires distributed to MSME and startup leaders and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with Smart PLS. The results indicate that Digital Technology Adoption, Digital Training and Development, and Work Flexibility do not significantly influence workforce productivity or organizational performance (p > 0.05). However, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention and the Utilization of HR Analytics and AI have a significant and positive impact on both workforce productivity and performance outcomes (p = 0.000). These findings highlight that while not all digital HR strategies yield immediate benefits, the ability to build dynamic capabilities through innovative talent practices and data-driven HR systems is essential to achieving competitive advantage and organizational success in the digital economy.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Customer data access and fintech entry: Early evidence from open banking
hot.abstract: Open banking (OB) empowers bank customers to share their financial transaction data with fintechs and other banks. New cross-country data shows 49 countries adopted OB policies, privacy preferences predict policy adoption, and adoption spurs fintech entry. UK microdata shows that OB enables: (i) consumers to access both financial advice and credit; (ii) SMEs to establish new lending relationships. In a calibrated model, OB universally improves welfare through entry and product improvements when used for advice. When used for credit, OB promotes entry and competition by reducing adverse selection, but higher prices for costlier or privacy-conscious consumers partially offset these benefits.

hot.title: AI-Driven Financial Transparency and Corporate Governance: Enhancing Accounting Practices with Evidence from Jordan
hot.abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into financial transparency and corporate governance has reshaped how organizations ensure accountability, regulatory compliance, and risk management. This study examines the impact of AI-driven financial transparency on corporate governance and regulatory reform, focusing on Jordan. Utilizing a stratified random sampling approach, data were collected from 564 corporate professionals across key economic sectors. Statistical analyses, including structural equation modeling (SEM) and multiple regression analysis, reveal that AI adoption significantly enhances corporate governance effectiveness (R2 = 0.582), improves risk management (R2 = 0.502), and increases stakeholder engagement (R2 = 0.681). AI also facilitates regulatory compliance by automating monitoring processes and reducing human errors in financial disclosures. However, challenges such as bias in AI algorithms, data privacy concerns, and the need for regulatory adaptation persist. These findings contribute to the body of knowledge on AI-driven governance and provide insights for policymakers and corporate leaders.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: Effect of anthropomorphism and perceived intelligence in chatbot avatars of visual design on user experience: accounting for perceived empathy and trust
hot.abstract: Introduction The rapid advancement of intelligent chatbots has transformed human-AI interaction, offering novel opportunities to enhance user experience (UX) through psychological and design interventions. However, the mechanisms by which chatbot design features influence UX remain understudied, particularly regarding the roles of emotional and cognitive mediators. Methods This study employed a 2 × 2 within-subjects experimental design with 160 participants to investigate the effects of anthropomorphism (high vs. low) and perceived intelligence (high vs. low) in chatbot avatars on UX. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was utilized to analyze the mediating roles of perceived empathy and trust in this relationship. Results Direct effects of anthropomorphism and perceived intelligence on UX were nonsignificant. However, their combined influence was significantly mediated by perceived empathy and trust ( β = 0.48, * p * < 0.01). Specifically, highly anthropomorphic avatars correlated with elevated empathy ( β = 0.32) and trust ( β = 0.27), which in turn improved UX. Discussion These findings underscore the importance of emotional engagement over mere intelligence in designing effective chatbots. This research contributes unique insights into the complex mechanisms governing user interactions with intelligent chatbots, emphasizing the need for design strategies that prioritize emotional connections and cognitive ease.

hot.title: The multinational enterprise, capabilities, and digitalization: governance and growth with world disorder
hot.abstract: Abstract This essay revisits my 2014 JIBS article about the potential for integrating international business internalization theory with a strategic management capabilities perspective. It recaps the capabilities framework with an emphasis on the learning required of emerging market multinationals and illustrates this with the case of Hyundai Motor Company’s internationalization and growth. It also discusses two aspects of the global economy that have become more prominent since 2014 in shaping international business: geopolitical uncertainty and digitalization. A rise in geopolitical tensions appears to be rebalancing the relationships between multinationals and home/host governments. Digitalization facilitates international business; but it adds new vulnerabilities by (further) accelerating competition, enabling new rivals, and introducing systemic risks into digital supply chains. Implications for managers, board members, and international business scholars are drawn.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing Within the Framework of Sustainable Management
hot.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not only revolutionizing digital marketing through personalized customer experiences and optimized advertising strategies, but it is also contributing to sustainability initiatives. As AI reshapes digital marketing, its impact on sustainability is becoming increasingly significant. This dynamic highlights the necessity of exploring how AI can be utilized to foster more sustainable marketing practices. This study seeks to answer the pivotal question: “How does AI impact the sustainability of digital marketing?” A systematic literature review was conducted in this study, following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework to identify various relevant articles in the areas of sustainability and marketing. Furthermore, this study examines the crucial role of AI in enhancing sustainable business practices, highlighting a significant increase in adoption among enterprises. The findings demonstrate that the effective integration of AI into digital marketing enhances environmental sustainability, supports the attainment of economic sustainability objectives, and contributes positively to social sustainability outcomes. This study contributes to the field by providing a comprehensive analysis of the intersection between AI and sustainable marketing practices and offers valuable insights for marketers, businesses, and policymakers.

latest.title: Destructive Leadership: The Hidden Cost To People And Organizations
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Destructive leadership represents a significant organizational phenomenon whose consequences extend beyond the immediate interaction between leaders and employees and may exert a sustained influence on organizational climate and culture. This article examines the mechanisms through which destructive leadership behaviours manifest at the organizational level, with particular emphasis on changes in communication, trust and perceived fairness, role clarity, workload, recognition systems, and the gradual establishment of dysfunctional norms and behavioural patterns. Organizational climate and organizational culture are analysed as interrelated but conceptually distinct levels through which the consequences of destructive leadership can be identified. Finally, the article discusses practical approaches to the early recognition, prevention, and mitigation of its impact on employees and organizations.

latest.title: Kepemimpinan Transformasional, Kepuasan Kerja, dan Kinerja Karyawan: Peran Mediasi Komitmen Organisasi pada Suku Dinas Tenaga Kerja, Transmigrasi, dan Energi Kota Jakarta Utara
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi dan Manajemen Indonesia
latest.abstract: Kinerja Karyawan pada instansi pelayanan publik berkaitan dengan kepemimpinan atasan, kepuasan kerja, dan komitmen pegawai terhadap organisasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji pengaruh kepemimpinan transformasional dan kepuasan kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan serta peran komitmen organisasi sebagai variabel mediasi pada Suku Dinas Tenaga Kerja, Transmigrasi, dan Energi Kota Administrasi Jakarta Utara. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif melalui survei kuesioner dengan skala Likert 1–4 terhadap seluruh pegawai pada lima unit kerja (sensus; N = 100), setelah pretest terhadap 34 pegawai di luar sampel utama. Data dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan SmartPLS 4. Hasil evaluasi model pengukuran menunjukkan bahwa seluruh konstruk memenuhi kriteria validitas dan reliabilitas, dengan AVE sebesar 0,600–0,783 dan composite reliability sebesar 0,899–0,940. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa kepemimpinan transformasional (β = 0,468) dan kepuasan kerja (β = 0,394) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Kinerja Karyawan. Kepuasan kerja juga berpengaruh positif terhadap komitmen organisasi (β = 0,607), sedangkan kepemimpinan transformasional tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap komitmen organisasi (β = −0,059). Komitmen organisasi berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Kinerja Karyawan (β = 0,487) serta memediasi pengaruh kepuasan kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan (β = 0,174), tetapi tidak memediasi pengaruh kepemimpinan transformasional terhadap Kinerja Karyawan. Dengan demikian, lima hipotesis didukung (H1, H2, H4, H5, dan H7), sedangkan H3 dan H6 tidak didukung. Temuan ini menunjukkan pentingnya kepemimpinan transformasional, kepuasan kerja, dan komitmen organisasi dalam mendukung kinerja pegawai pada instansi

latest.title: Model AISAS dalam Proses Pembentukan Loyalitas Pelanggan pada Akun @Warunghasturi
latest.abstract: Perkembangan media sosial mendorong pelaku usaha kuliner memanfaatkan komunikasi pemasaran digital untuk menarik perhatian konsumen dan mempertahankan loyalitas pelanggan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis komunikasi pemasaran digital melalui akun Instagram @warunghasturi berdasarkan model Attention, Interest, Search, Action, dan Share (AISAS) serta mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor pendukung pelaksanaannya dalam meningkatkan loyalitas pelanggan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan pengumpulan data melalui observasi, wawancara terstruktur, dan dokumentasi. Informan terdiri atas enam orang yang meliputi pemilik usaha, admin Instagram, pekerja, pengikut Instagram, dan konsumen. Data dianalisis menggunakan model interaktif Miles dan Huberman melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Warung Hasturi telah menerapkan kelima tahapan AISAS melalui konten visual, informasi produk, interaksi dengan pengikut, promosi, dan unggahan pengalaman pelanggan. Faktor pendukungnya meliputi konsistensi pengelolaan konten, kreativitas dan keragaman unggahan, interaksi dua arah, serta penyampaian informasi dan promosi produk. Loyalitas pelanggan terlihat dari pembelian ulang, kunjungan kembali, dan rekomendasi kepada orang lain. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa komunikasi pemasaran digital melalui Instagram dapat mendukung loyalitas pelanggan apabila diimbangi dengan kualitas produk, pelayanan, kenyamanan outlet, dan kesiapan operasional usaha.

latest.title: Influence of ROA, Working Capital to Total Asset dan Debt Ratio to Market Book Value in ASEAN Countries
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the influence of financial performance on the value of non-financial firms in ASEAN countries. In this study, financial performance is proxied by Return on Assets (ROA), the Working Capital to Total Asset, and the Debt Ratio, while firm value is proxied by the Market-to-Book Value (MBV). The data analysis technique employed is multiple linear regression. The study population consists of 223 firms, with a sample of 146 firms. The sampled firms are distributed as follows: 15 from Singapore, 11 from Indonesia, 17 from the Philippines, 33 from Thailand, and 70 from Malaysia. Data collection was conducted using purposive sampling. The results indicate that Return on Assets (ROA) significantly influences the Market-to-Book Value (MBV), as evidenced by a significance value of 0.002 (which is less than 0.05), suggesting a positive impact of ROA on MBV. The Working Capital to Total Assets (WCTA) ratio does not significantly influence the Market-to-Book Value (MBV), with a significance value of 0.757 (greater than 0.05). Similarly, the Debt Ratio does not show a significant influence on MBV, with a significance value of 0.911. The ANOVA significance value is 0.021, indicating that ROA, WCTA, and the Debt Ratio collectively influence the MBV. The R² value is 0.254, meaning that ROA, WCTA, and the Debt Ratio account for 25.4% of the variance in MBV, while the remaining 74.6% is influenced by other variables. This suggests that a firm's ability to meet its short-term obligations is not yet a significant factor influencing the market's assessment of the firm's value.

latest.title: When Pixels Persuade: Virtual Influencer Content Appeals, Credibility, and Generation Z Purchase Intention
latest.abstract: This study investigates how the emotional, rational and authenticity appeals of virtual influencer (VI) content, together with VI credibility, shape Generation Z purchase intention through perceived content value and consumer engagement. An online survey was conducted among Indonesian Generation Z Instagram users who had been exposed to Lil Miquela’s Calvin Klein content, and the proposed model was estimated using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that rational appeal, emotional appeal and VI credibility are positively associated with perceived content value, whereas authenticity appeal shows no significant relationship. Perceived content value is positively related to consumer engagement, which in turn is positively related to purchase intention. Perceived content value mediates the relationships of rational appeal, emotional appeal and VI credibility with engagement, and engagement mediates the link between perceived content value and purchase intention. The study extends advertising value and source credibility perspectives to non-human endorsers by demonstrating that message characteristics and source evaluations operate jointly in VI marketing. For practitioners, the findings highlight the importance of informative, emotionally relevant and credible VI content. The cross-sectional, single-influencer and single-brand design limits causal inference and generalisability.

latest.title: Peran Financial self-efficacy dalam Memoderasi Literasi Keuangan Digital, Herding behavior, dan Perilaku Keuangan Mahasiswa
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of digital financial literacy and herding behavior on financial behavior, as well as to examine the role of financial self-efficacy as a moderating variable. The study sample consisted of economics education students from State University of Malang and State University of Surabaya. Data were collected using questionnaires. A quantitative approach was employed, utilizing multiple linear regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The results indicate that digital financial literacy has a positive and significant effect on financial behavior, whereas herding behavior has a negative and significant effect. Moderation analysis reveals that financial self-efficacy strengthens the impact of digital financial literacy on financial behavior and weakens the impact of herding behavior on financial behavior. These findings suggest that enhancing digital financial literacy can foster better financial behavior, while the tendency to follow others' financial decisions can diminish the quality of financial behavior.

latest.title: Cognitive networks reconstruct mindsets about STEM subjects and educational contexts in high-schoolers, undergraduates, experts and their digital twins
latest.abstract: Attitudes toward STEM develop from the interaction of conceptual knowledge, educational experiences, and affect. Here we use cognitive network science to reconstruct group mindsets as behavioural forma mentis networks (BFMNs). In this case, nodes are cue words and free associations, edges are empirical associative links, and each concept is annotated with perceived valence. We analyse BFMNs from $$N=981$$ observations spanning high school students, university students, and early-career STEM experts, alongside LLM (GPT-OSS) “digital twins” (group-level synthetic counterparts, not individual-level copies), prompted to emulate comparable profiles. Focusing also on semantic neighbourhoods (“frames”) around key target concepts (e.g., STEM subjects or educational actors/places), we quantify frames in terms of valence auras, emotional profiles, network overlap (Jaccard similarity), and concreteness relative to null baselines. Across student groups, science and research are consistently framed positively, while their core quantitative subjects (mathematics and statistics) exhibit more negative and anxiety-related auras, amplified in higher math-anxiety subgroups, evidencing a STEM-science cognitive and emotional dissonance. High-anxiety frames are also less concrete than chance, suggesting more abstract and decontextualised representations of threatening quantitative domains. Human networks show greater overlap between mathematics and anxiety than GPT-OSS. The results highlight how BFMNs capture cognitive-affective signatures of mindsets towards the target domains and indicate that these synthetic counterparts approximate cultural attitudes but miss key context-sensitive, experience-based components of human educational anxiety.

latest.title: Network analysis of serious leisure and life satisfaction
latest.abstract: Serious leisure refers to the systematic pursuit of leisure activities that offer meaningful engagement and personal fulfilment. Although previous studies have shown that serious leisure is positively associated with life satisfaction, less is known about how its specific qualities and rewards are interrelated and how they are positioned within the broader relational structure surrounding life satisfaction. This study employed network analysis to examine the conditional associations among serious leisure components and life satisfaction among individuals engaged in cycling as a form of serious leisure. A regularised partial correlation network was estimated, and supplementary structural equation modelling was conducted to examine whether nodes directly connected to life satisfaction retained their associations. The results confirmed a positive association between serious leisure and life satisfaction, with several rewards and seriousness nodes showing direct connections to life satisfaction. In the network, financial return, unique ethos, group maintenance, group attraction, career contingencies, and re-creation were directly connected to life satisfaction. However, only financial return and group maintenance retained significant associations in the supplementary model. Ethos, self-actualisation, and identification with pursuit also appeared important as key nodes within the broader serious leisure structure. These findings suggest that life satisfaction may be better understood not only through isolated serious leisure components, but also through the wider configuration of serious leisure qualities and rewards. Rather than suggesting that the association between serious leisure and life satisfaction reflects only stronger commitment, the findings point to a more nuanc

latest.title: Analysis of sleep quality and associated factors in patients with metabolic syndrome: a retrospective cross-sectional study
latest.abstract: Abstract Background The relationships of metabolic syndrome (MetS) with objective sleep architecture and continuity remain unclear. We examined these associations in inpatients undergoing polysomnography (PSG) and explored clinical and biochemical correlates of sleep efficiency (SE) within the MetS group. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 219 adults (97 with MetS; 122 without MetS). Generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, smoking, alcohol consumption, and the apnea–hypopnea index (AHI), modeled as ln(AHI + 1). Multiple comparisons were controlled using the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR). Additional analyses adjusted for body mass index (BMI), restricted AHI to an overlapping range, or replaced ln(AHI + 1) with raw AHI. Clinical and biochemical correlates of SE were explored within the MetS group. Results After adjustment, MetS was associated with lower SE (difference − 5.55% points, 95% confidence interval [CI] − 10.55 to − 0.55; P = 0.0297; q = 0.0415), higher N1 (4.36% points, 0.78 to 7.95; P = 0.0171; q = 0.0299), lower N3 (− 3.36% points, − 6.02 to − 0.71; P = 0.0131; q = 0.0299), longer wake after sleep onset (mean ratio 1.406, 1.073 to 1.844; P = 0.0135; q = 0.0299), and a higher arousal index (incidence rate ratio 1.265, 1.076 to 1.487; P = 0.0044; q = 0.0299). These associations remained significant after FDR correction; N2 ( P = 0.1787; q = 0.1959) and rapid eye movement sleep ( P = 0.1959; q = 0.1959) did not. Most associations weakened after BMI adjustment. SE was sensitive to a single influential observation. All five associations remained significant after FDR correction among patients with 5 ≤ AHI < 45 events/h. latest.title: Process mining of breast cancer care pathways from routine electronic medical records: coordination patterns, transition-time variation, and hospital-level differences
latest.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Breast cancer care involves multiple services over several months, yet most research has focused on individual treatment components. As a result, we still know relatively little about how clinical and coordination events are sequenced across services in routine practice. Linked electronic medical record (EMR) data and process mining provide an opportunity to reconstruct these patient-level pathways. This study aims to characterise breast cancer care pathways, identify recurring coordination patterns and transition-time variation, and examine their associations with measured clinical characteristics and treating hospital. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted using linked EMR data from 686 patients with invasive breast cancer who underwent surgery within the Illawarra Shoalhaven Local Health District, Australia, between 2010 and 2014. Patient-level pathways spanning diagnosis, care coordination and treatment initiation events during the initial treatment episode were reconstructed from three routine clinical information systems using process mining. Coordination patterns were classified as MDT-led or Referral-led based on the relative timing of multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion and oncology referral. Transition times between care events were quantified, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with coordination pattern and pre-treatment oncology consultation. Results The event log contained 4,175 timestamped events and 143 distinct pathway variants. Among these variants, 81 (56.6%) were observed in only one patient each. Despite this patient-level heterogeneity, two recurring coordination patterns accounted for most patients: MDT-led, in which MDT discussion occurred before or on the same date as

latest.title: Development of a Digital Violence Prevention E-Module to Strengthen Harmonious Social Interaction among Elementary School Students
latest.abstract: Abstract Violence in elementary schools in Indonesia is still a serious problem that hinders student development. This research aims to develop an E-Mode of Violence Prevention Education designed to strengthen the harmonization of harmonious life in the elementary school environment. This study uses a 4D development model which includes the Define, Design, Develop and Disseminate stages which involve the validation of experts, teachers and students in four elementary schools in Gorontalo Regency. The results of expert validation show that the E-Module meets the criteria of "very valid" with an average score above 85%. The limited trial showed that more than 85% of students rated the E-Module as practical, easy to use, and attractive. Data analysis through the Kolmogorov–Smirnov normality test showed that the pretest and posttest data were normally distributed (Sig.>0.05). The results of the paired samples t-test showed significant differences in students' knowledge, attitudes, and skills before and after the use of the E-Module (p = 0.001). The effect size calculation (Cohen's d) ranged from 1.34–1.86 with a very large category, which confirms the strong influence of the E-Module in improving the competence of violence prevention. Thus, this E-Module is valid, practical, and effective, and is able to be widely implemented as part of creating harmonious harmony of life in the elementary school environment.

latest.title: Nocturnal sleep duration and incident slow gait in a cohort of Chinese older adults over 4 years
latest.abstract: Gait speed is a core marker of physical function in older adults. This study aimed to examine the longitudinal associations of nocturnal sleep duration and sleep quality with incident slow gait in a cohort of Chinese older adults. We analyzed data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) 2011 baseline and 2015 follow-up. Participants aged ≥ 60 years with normal gait speed at baseline were included. Sleep duration was categorized as short (< 6 h), normal (6–8 h), or long (> 8 h). Sleep quality was classified as good/fair or poor based on self-report. Incident slow gait was defined as gait speed falling below one sex- and age-group-specific standard deviation of the mean at follow-up. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Of 3,195 participants, 441 (13.8%) developed incident slow gait over 4 years. Compared with normal sleep duration, short sleep duration (< 6 h) was associated with higher odds of incident slow gait in the fully adjusted model (OR = 1.24, 95% CI 1.00–1.54, P = 0.050). Long sleep duration and poor sleep quality showed no significant association with incident slow gait in the fully adjusted model. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant interaction modification by sex, age, education, marital status, or residence. Short nocturnal sleep duration (< 6 h) was associated with higher odds of incident slow gait in a cohort of Chinese older adults after adjustment for measured covariates. However, this association was of borderline statistical significance and was not statistically significant in the fully adjusted survey-weighted analysis; these findings should therefore be interpreted with caution.

latest.title: Workplace bullying among healthcare workers: reporting, organisational resolution, and associations with mental health and work productivity
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Workplace bullying is common in healthcare and is associated with adverse psychological and occupational consequences. However, less is known about reporting, organisational resolution, and their relationship with mental health and work productivity. This study examined these pathways across a broad healthcare workforce. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 516 healthcare workers in a Nigerian teaching hospital, including clinical, technical, administrative, and ancillary personnel. Workplace bullying was assessed using the Negative Acts Questionnaire-Revised, mental health using the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales, and work productivity using the Healthcare Productivity Survey. Chi-square tests, independent-samples t -tests, multivariable logistic regression, and one-way analysis of variance were used. Results Among 516 healthcare workers, 267 (51.7%) met the criterion for workplace bullying. Depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms were present in 51.6%, 58.7%, and 31.0%, respectively. Among those experiencing bullying, 197 (73.8%) did not report it. Of the 70 who reported, 21 (30.0%) reported no action, 23 (32.9%) were dissatisfied with the action taken, and 26 (37.1%) were satisfied with the organisational response. Male workers and supervisors were more likely to report bullying, while clinical workers and those with longer employment duration were less likely to report. Reporting was also more likely when bullying was perpetrated by colleagues than superiors. Reporting was more common when bullying involved physically intimidating behaviours than work-related and person-related bullying. latest.title: Social Commerce Adoption and MSME Marketing Performance: The Mediating Role of Digital Trust and the Moderating Role of Digital Literacy
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh adopsi social commerce terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM melalui peran mediasi kepercayaan digital, serta menguji peran moderasi literasi digital pada hubungan antara adopsi social commerce dan kepercayaan digital. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan populasi UMKM sektor kuliner, fesyen, dan kerajinan di Kota Surakarta yang telah mengadopsi social commerce. Sampel ditentukan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling dengan jumlah 150 responden UMKM. Data dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) melalui perangkat lunak SmartPLS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa adopsi social commerce berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM maupun terhadap kepercayaan digital, kepercayaan digital berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM, serta kepercayaan digital terbukti memediasi secara parsial pengaruh adopsi social commerce terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM. Namun, literasi digital tidak terbukti memoderasi pengaruh adopsi social commerce terhadap kepercayaan digital. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi teoritis melalui penerapan kerangka Stimulus-Organism-Response pada konteks transformasi digital UMKM, serta implikasi praktis bahwa penguatan kepercayaan digital merupakan strategi kunci bagi UMKM dalam mengoptimalkan manfaat social commerce, sementara literasi digital lebih berperan sebagai prediktor langsung dibandingkan faktor penguat.

latest.title: A Comparative Analysis Of Academic Buoyancy Among Higher Secondary School Students On The Basis Of Gender
latest.abstract: Academic buoyancy refers to students’ capacity to manage ordinary academic setbacks, such as disappointing marks, examination pressure, difficult assignments, competing deadlines, and critical feedback. The present study examined academic buoyancy among higher secondary school students in relation to gender. A quantitative, cross-sectional, descriptive-comparative design was used. This study reported the sample of 300 students (150 male and 150 female) in Tehsil Sahiwal and Tehsil Shahpur, District Sargodha. Academic buoyancy was measured through a 20-item questionnaire covering composure, confidence, coordination, commitment, and control; the reported pilot reliability was Cronbach’s alpha = .830. The gender table showed that 54.0% of male students, compared with 41.3% of female students, were classified in the upper two buoyancy categories (very good or excellent). A chi-square test of the five-category gender distribution was not statistically significant. The equivalent one-way analysis of variance was also not significant, F (1, 298) = 3.03, p = .083.

latest.title: Psychological Capital And Academic Achievement Among Secondary School Students: A Correlational Study
latest.abstract: This study examined psychological capital and academic achievement among Grade 10 students in government secondary schools in Tehsil Sahiwal, District Sargodha, Pakistan. A quantitative survey approach was used to describe students’ psychological capital and examine its relationship with academic achievement. The study focused on four psychological-capital dimensions: self-efficacy, confidence, hope, resilience, and optimism. A researcher-developed 17-item questionnaire was reviewed by experts and pilot tested with 70 students; the reported Cronbach’s alpha was .742. Students’ academic achievement was intended to be represented by annual examination marks from school records, while the questionnaire also contained four self-reported academic-achievement items. The correlation matrix contains an apparent perfect correlation between optimism and the questionnaire’s academic-achievement score (r = 1.000, p < .001), whereas the reported association between recorded marks and the academic-achievement score was small and nonsignificant (r = −.078, p = .161).

latest.title: A Study on the Factors Influencing Foreign Direct Investment in Indonesia
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: Foreign direct investment (FDI) can serve developing countries as a basis for accelerating investment and economic growth. Many developing countries need large amounts of development capital while national revenues remain too low. This study aims to determine which factors affect FDI in Indonesia. Using panel data for 34 Indonesian provinces over 2017–2022, it estimates a random effects panel regression model in STATA, with data from Bank Indonesia, the Central Bureau of Statistics, the Ministry of Trade and other official websites. The results show that import value and export value have a significant positive effect on FDI and the exchange rate has a significant negative effect, whereas gross regional product and labor force have no significant effect. Based on these findings, the study proposes corresponding policy recommendations.

latest.title: Community-Based Tourism Projects and Local Community Livelihoods. A Case of Nyungwe Community Guide Project in Nyamasheke District, Rwanda
latest.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
latest.abstract: This study examined the effect of community-based tourism projects on local community livelihoods in Nyamasheke District, with reference to the Nyungwe Community Guide Project.Specifically, the study attempted to assess the effect of stakeholders' networks in the Nyungwe Community Guide Project on local community livelihoods in Nyamasheke District.The study was guided by Stakeholder Theory, which explains the importance of relationships, coordination, information sharing, and resource exchange among actors who influence or are affected by a project.A descriptive-correlational research design was adopted using a quantitative approach supported by qualitative information from the study context.The target population comprised 272 respondents, from which a sample size of 162 respondents was determined, while 154 questionnaires were distributed and 142 were returned, giving a questionnaire response rate of 92.2%.Data were collected using structured questionnaires and interviews, and quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analysis; a single-predictor regression interpretation was also developed from the reported bivariate correlation.Findings from the questionnaire showed high agreement that stakeholder networks supported project effectiveness, access to resources, information sharing, community engagement, and local livelihood improvement.Pearson correlation analysis showed a strong positive and statistically significant relationship between stakeholder networks and local community livelihoods (r = .773,p < .001).The study therefore concluded that stronger stakeholder networks were associated with better livelihood outcomes among communities linked to the Nyungwe Community Guide Project.The study recommends strengthening coordina

latest.title: The Role of Customer Satisfaction In Mediating The Effect of Service Performance and Perceived Value On Customer Loyalty: Evidence From A B2B Outsourced Cleaning Service In A Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Setting
latest.venue: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Outsourced facility services have become a strategic component of operations in Indonesia's highly regulated pharmaceutical industry, where cleanliness is not a cosmetic concern but a compliance requirement embedded in CPOB, WHO Prequalification, ISO 9001:2015, and ISO 14001:2015 standards. This study examined why an outsourced cleaning-service provider operating exclusively for a single pharmaceutical client since 2013 recorded 38 client complaints between November 2025 and January 2026, of which 66% concerned Service Performance and Perceived Value, and asked whether Customer Satisfaction mediates the effects of these two constructs on Customer Loyalty. Prior research has largely tested this chain in consumer-facing settings, leaving the business-to-business, compliance-driven pharmaceutical outsourcing context empirically unexamined. A quantitative, explanatory cross-sectional survey collected primary data from 355 employees of PT Bio Farma (Persero) Pasteur, Bandung, drawn by simple random sampling from a population of 3,096 and analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS. All eight hypotheses were supported at the 5% significance level. The model explained 74.0% of the variance in Customer Satisfaction and 68.3% of the variance in Customer Loyalty. Service Performance showed the strongest association with Customer Satisfaction (β = 0.543; f² = 0.901), while Customer Satisfaction showed the strongest association with Customer Loyalty (β = 0.494) and partially mediated both upstream paths (indirect effects β = 0.269 and β = 0.229). The study empirically extends the satisfaction-mediation framework to regulated B2B outsourcing and indicates that satisfaction management should be the central lever in loyalty-building strategy.

latest.title: The Monitoring Paradox: Why Oversight Mechanisms Fail to Predict PPP Infrastructure Projects Performance in Kenya
latest.abstract: Purpose: The study explored role of project monitoring mechanisms in enhancing performance of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) infrastructure projects in Kenya. Policy puts a lot of emphasis on the need for monitoring along the project lifecycle; however, many PPP projects continue to display inefficiencies pointing towards weak monitoring systems. Materials and Methods: Data were collected from 252 respondents representing government agencies, private consortia, and project management units across 103 PPP projects. Regression analysis was used to test relationship between project monitoring mechanisms and project performance. Findings: Project monitoring had a statistically significant but weak positive influence on project performance (β = .014, p < .005). The positive but not so profound effect suggests that the monitoring frameworks that exists are largely compliance-oriented rather than the one that drives performance in the project environment. Implications to Theory, Practice and Policy: The study recommends institutionalizing real-time monitoring, feedback systems, and adoption of digital data tools to strengthen accountability within PPP infrastructure projects in Kenya. To anchor these measures, the Public Private Partnerships Act, 2021 and the regulations around privately funded public infrastructure should be amended to create a performance-based monitoring making it mandatory. This includes standardization of KPIs, periodic independent performance reviews, and public disclosure of monitoring reports across the project lifecycle. Keywords: Monitoring Mechanisms, PPP, Infrastructure Performance, Project Governance, Kenya

latest.title: Perancangan Booklet sebagai Media Promosi Wisata Edukasi Susu di Desa Padusan, Kabupaten Mojokerto
latest.venue: KOMUNITA Jurnal Pengabdian dan Pemberdayaan Masyarakat
latest.abstract: Desa Padusan, Kabupaten Mojokerto, memiliki potensi wisata edukasi berbasis pengolahan susu, tetapi potensi tersebut belum didukung oleh media promosi yang terintegrasi dan menarik secara visual. Program pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan merancang booklet sebagai media edukasi dan promosi wisata pengolahan susu di Padusan. Program menggunakan pendekatan Design Thinking melalui lima tahap: Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, dan Testing. Identifikasi kebutuhan dan evaluasi produk dilakukan melalui wawancara dan diskusi dengan Dinas Pariwisata dan Kebudayaan setempat serta kuesioner kepada responden masyarakat. Luaran berupa booklet 10 halaman yang menyajikan perawatan sapi perah, pemerahan, pengecekan mutu susu, pengemasan dan pemasaran, serta produk olahan susu. Pengujian kepada 40 responden dan evaluasi Dinas Pariwisata dan Kebudayaan menunjukkan bahwa booklet dinilai informatif, menarik, mudah dipahami, dan relevan dengan promosi wisata saat ini. Responden berasal dari kelompok usia yang beragam dengan dominasi Generasi Z. Booklet juga memenuhi kriteria evaluasi SMART dan berpotensi menjadi media promosi praktis untuk mendukung wisata edukasi dan kuliner di Desa Padusan.Booklet; Promosi Pariwisata; Wisata Edukasi; Pengolahan Susu; Design Thinking

latest.title: Hybrid intelligent modeling for calibrated business and financial risk classification: a decision-support perspective
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a calibration-aware hybrid framework for large-scale business and financial risk classification, addressing heterogeneous features, nonlinear relationships, temporal distribution shifts, class imbalance and unreliable probability estimates. Design/methodology/approach The hybrid multi-agent quantum neural transformer (H–MAQNT) combines a tabular transformer, domain-specialized variational quantum neural network (VQNN) agents and adaptive attention-based fusion. It uses leakage-controlled preprocessing, domain-informed features, imbalance-aware training, validation-only model selection and calibration and quantum-aware multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization (QMFBO) for cost-aware tuning. Findings On temporally held-out LendingClub and IEEE–CIS future test periods, H–MAQNT outperforms strong gradient-boosted, neural and transformer-based baselines in discrimination and probability quality. It improves the receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC–AUC) by approximately 1.1–1.3 percentage points over the strongest Transformer-based baselines, lowers expected calibration error (ECE) on both data sets and reduces high-fidelity optimization evaluations by 35% relative to single-fidelity Bayesian optimization. Research limitations/implications The evidence is based on two public data sets and classically simulated quantum circuits. Future work should test additional institutions, rolling time windows, physical hardware and prospective drift and recalibration policies. Practical implications Calibrated risk probabilities may support fraud-alert prioritization, risk ranking, threshold setting, and secondary review, helping institutions weigh predictive gains against computational cost. latest.title: Ansiedad y depresión asociados al nivel de riesgo en adolescentes en conflicto con la ley penal, Perú
latest.abstract: Objective: Determine the level of anxiety and depression associated with the level of risk of violence in teenagers in conflict with criminal law, in the city of Pucallpa, Peru. Materials and methods: Research grounded in the method deductive, type non-experimental. The methodology was supported at the explanatory level, also being an applied research with a non-experimental, cross-sectional design, as well as a cross-sectional descriptive one. The sample comprised a white population of 150 adolescents, from which 80 were randomly selected. The tests carried out to evaluate existing affective disorders were: the Zung test for anxiety and depression, as well as the Manual for the Structured Assessment of Risk of Violence in Young People (SAVRY). Results: The results show that there is no association between anxiety and depression and the level of risk of violence in teenagers; however, anxiety, although its mild frequency was at risk, was not associated with this characteristic, and depression presented a very high frequency without association. Conclusions: Therefore, it is concluded that depression does not have an association with the risk of violent behavior or, overall, with anxiety, which is why it was not determined to be a factor that increases the risk of violence.

latest.title: The Effect of Gamification Method on Mathematics toward Students Achievement of Fifth-Grade in Elementary Students
latest.venue: International Journal of Education Culture and Society
latest.abstract: The use of gamification in elementary mathematics instruction requires further examination to clarify its contribution to student achievement. This study examined the effect of gamification on the mathematics achievement of fifth-grade students at SD Negeri 7 Salotungo, Soppeng Regency. A quantitative approach was employed using a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design. Participants comprised 25 students from Class V.A as the experimental group and 23 students from Class V.B as the control group. Data were collected using an achievement test and analyzed through descriptive statistics and an independent-samples t-test. Descriptive results showed that the experimental group’s mean achievement score increased from 48.2 before the intervention to 76.4 after its implementation. The independent-samples t-test indicated a statistically significant difference between the groups (two-tailed p = .011). These findings suggest that gamification has potential to support mathematics achievement among fifth-grade students in this setting. The study contributes contextual evidence to research on gamification in elementary mathematics education and informs the consideration of interactive instructional strategies. Its practical implications concern the use of game mechanics, including points, levels, and leaderboards, to structure mathematics learning activities. Further research should investigate the long-term effects of gamified instruction and its application across other mathematical topics.

latest.title: Critical digital literacy, digital epistemic beliefs, and teachers’ instructional modeling of reasoning: Predictors of pre-service teachers’ online evaluative reading literacy
latest.venue: International Journal of Education Learning and Pedagogical Sciences (INJELPS)
latest.abstract: Aim: Digital environments increasingly require pre-service teachers to evaluate conflicting and potentially unreliable information.However, limited empirical evidence explains how critical digital literacy, digital epistemic beliefs, and teachers' instructional modeling of reasoning collectively relate to online evaluative reading literacy.This study examined these three variables as predictors of pre-service teachers' online evaluative reading literacy, particularly their abilities to judge the validity of ideas, identify bias and fairness, assess authorial purpose and intent, and make value judgments.Methodology: A descriptive-correlational research design was employed involving 227 fourth-year pre-service teachers from a private teacher education institution in Northern Mindanao, Philippines, selected through cluster random sampling.Data were collected using validated measures of the three predictor variables and an objective Online Evaluative Reading Literacy Assessment.Descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis were used to examine the data.Results: Findings revealed very high levels of critical digital literacy, digital epistemic beliefs, teachers' instructional modeling of reasoning, and online evaluative reading literacy, although judging the validity of ideas remained comparatively less developed.Multiple regression analysis showed that the three predictor variables collectively explained only 2.6% of the variance in online evaluative reading literacy (R² = .026).However, the overall regression model was not statistically significant, F(3, 223) = 1.963, p = .120.Furthermore, none of the three predictors individually demonstrated a statistically significant predictive relationship with online evaluative reading literacy.Conclusion: Online evaluative

latest.title: The Influence of Profitability, Interest Rates (BI Rate) and Institutional Ownership on Stock Returns at PT Akasha Wira Internasional Tbk
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationships between profitability, the Bank Indonesia policy interest rate, institutional ownership, and stock returns at PT Akasha Wira International Tbk over the 2013–2024 period. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data obtained from the company’s annual reports and Bank Indonesia publications. The dataset comprises 12 annual observations. Profitability was measured using return on assets (ROA), while institutional ownership was measured by the proportion of shares held by institutional investors. The interest-rate variable was based on Bank Indonesia’s published policy-rate series, taking into account changes in the official benchmark terminology during the observation period. Multiple linear regression and hypothesis testing were conducted using SPSS version 23. The results indicate that profitability is positively and significantly associated with stock returns (t = 4.476, p = 0.002), whereas the policy interest rate is negatively and significantly associated with stock returns (t = −2.830, p = 0.022). Institutional ownership does not exhibit a statistically significant partial association with stock returns (t = 1.803, p = 0.109). Simultaneously, the three independent variables are statistically significant in the regression model (F = 10.610, p = 0.004). The model yields an R-squared of 0.799, indicating that the predictors jointly account for 79.9% of the in-sample variation in stock returns, while the adjusted R-squared is 0.724 after accounting for the number of predictors and observations. Given the limited sample and single-company setting, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. This study provides case-specific evidence concerning the relationships between firm-level profitability, monetary policy, owner

latest.title: The Effect of Campus Image and Word of Mouth on Students' Decisions in Choosing a Business Education Study Program at State University Of Medan
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi, Manajemen dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of campus image and word of mouth on the decision of 2025 cohort students in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Universitas Negeri Medan. This research employed a quantitative approach using an ex post facto method. The population consisted of 111 students, all of whom were selected as the sample through the total sampling technique. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, and the coefficient of determination (R²). The results showed that campus image had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (t value = 7.322; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Word of mouth also had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (t value = 5.779; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Simultaneously, both variables had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (f value = 40.939; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). The findings indicate that 43.1% of the variation in students' decisions to choose the Business Education Study Program can be explained by campus image and word of mouth, while the remaining 56.9% is influenced by other factors outside the scope of this study.

latest.title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
latest.venue: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Economy and Management Study
latest.abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

latest.title: Enhancing English vocabulary acquisition through a flipped classroom model supported by USA learns: a quasi-experimental study with Colombian EFL learners
latest.abstract: Vocabulary acquisition constitutes a fundamental component of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning, as it directly influences learners’ communicative competence and academic performance. Despite its importance, many secondary school students experience difficulties in developing an adequate lexical repertoire, particularly in contexts where exposure to English is limited. This study aimed to determine the effect of a Flipped Classroom model supported by the USA Learns platform on English vocabulary acquisition among Colombian secondary school students. A quantitative approach framed within the positivist paradigm was adopted. The study employed a quasi-experimental design with non-equivalent groups, including an experimental group exposed to the Flipped Classroom intervention and a control group receiving traditional instruction. Vocabulary acquisition was measured through pre-test and post-test assessments designed to evaluate students’ lexical knowledge across multiple thematic categories aligned with Pre-A1, A1, and A2 proficiency levels of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). The findings revealed that students who participated in the Flipped Classroom intervention demonstrated a greater mean vocabulary gain (+2.5 points) than those in the control group (+0.5 points). Category-level results were mixed (see Table 2): the largest gains for the experimental group were observed in greetings, presentations and farewells (+5.27) and classroom vocabulary (+4.27), with small gains in personal information and numbers (+0.14) and cardinal and ordinal numbers (+0.55), while means decreased in the categories of verb To be, calendar, parts of the day, and daily routine and time. The results suggest that combining flipped learning principles wi

latest.title: Collaborative Governance Dalam Pengembangan Pariwisata di Gunung Kidul
latest.venue: Jurnal Akuntansi Ekonomi dan Manajemen Bisnis
latest.abstract: Karst-based natural tourism in Gunungkidul Regency has become one of the key drivers of regional economic growth. However, the management of karst destinations involves multiple actors with diverse interests, including the Tourism Office, private sector, and local communities, thereby requiring an analysis of collaborative governance. This study focuses on three main destinations: Goa Jomblang, Kali Suci, and Gunungkidul Beach. The study adopted a qualitative case study approach. Data were gathered through in-depth interviews, field observations, and document analysis, and subsequently analyzed using the collaborative governance framework developed by Ansell and Gash (2008), which encompasses starting conditions, institutional design, facilitative leadership, and the collaborative process and intermediate outcomes. The results indicate variations in collaboration typologies according to the dominant actor. Goa Jomblang reflects an investor-driven collaboration model characterized by private sector dominance and limited community involvement as labor. Kali Suci demonstrates a community-driven collaboration rooted in social trust and mutual cooperation through Pokdarwis, representing the closest form to the ideal model of collaboration. Meanwhile, Gunungkidul Beach illustrates a government-driven collaboration under the dominance of the Tourism Office through bureaucratic systems, although local communities are still engaged in a shifting management scheme. The success of collaborative governance in karst tourism is influenced by the strength of social capital, governance certainty, facilitative leadership, community access to authority, benefit-sharing mechanisms, and the support of digital technology. The implications of this study highlight the need to strengthen commu

latest.title: The Impact of Shariah Governance and Its Consequences on CSR Disclosure: Evidence from Islamic Banks in Bangladesh
latest.venue: International Journal of Science and Business
latest.abstract: The purpose of current study is to reveal the level of CSRD practices of the Islamic banks operating in Bangladesh as well as to investigate the influence of Shariah Governance (SG) factors on CSR disclosure practices. To collect data for this study a nine-dimensional testable disclosure index was prepared on the basis of AAOIFI, Governance Standard No. 7, 2010 and from prior studies. Then data were collected from 8 Islamic banks for 10 years span ranging from 2013 to 2022 comprising 80 observations through content analysis of the annual reports available in the sampled banks websites. Each line of the annual report has been examined to identify whether any bank reveals CSR data specified in the CSRD index and if they do then receive a score of (1); if not, receive a score of (0). However, to analyze the panel data set the study employed OLS regression model to test the relationship among the hypothesized variables and generated descriptive statistics by using STATA Software version 16. The data analysis result reveals a relatively high level of CSR disclosure (66.36%) practices in the sampled Islamic banks. Moreover, it has been found that variables of SG included in this study explain about 72% of CSRD practices of sampled Islamic banks. The study also finds that board size, SSB size, and number of independent directors in the board have significant positive influence on CSRD. On the other, AC size, cross membership of board members show significant negative influence on CSRD. But, the result of gender composition and AC meeting indicate insignificant negative influence on CSRD. Thus, findings of this study provide new insights about the role of shariah governance in enhancing CSRD practices among the shariah based banks of Bangladesh and as such help improve their ov

latest.title: Bank complaint resolution outcomes and customer behavioural biases for accountable financial institutions in guwahati India
latest.venue: International Journal of Marketing Research Innovation
latest.abstract: Customer complaints against banks in India have risen sharply with the spread of digital banking, and accountable and transparent grievance redressal has become central to consumer protection and strong institutions. Earlier studies linked complaint handling to satisfaction and loyalty but paid little attention to how the outcome of a resolved complaint shapes the customer's later judgement. This study examines the influence of bank complaint resolution outcomes on four post-resolution behavioural biases: confirmation bias, loss aversion, overconfidence and complaint avoidance. Primary data were collected through a cross-sectional survey using a structured questionnaire from 547 customers across 329 branches of 12 public- and 12 private-sector banks in Guwahati City, India, who had lodged a formal complaint and were analysed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha and simple linear regression. The results show that 56.3% of complaints were fully resolved, 40.0% partially resolved, and 3.7% not resolved, and that the bias scales were reliable (α = 0.781 to 0.893). Complaint resolution outcome was positively related to confirmation bias (β = 0.764, R² = 0.584), loss aversion (β = 0.808, R² = 0.652) and overconfidence (β = 0.663, R² = 0.440), and negatively related to complaint avoidance (β = −0.783, R² = 0.613), all at p < 0.001. Loss aversion recorded the highest mean score (3.88) and confirmation bias the lowest (2.68). The findings suggest that complaint resolution outcomes account for 44.0% to 65.2% of the variation in post-resolution behavioural biases, indicating that resolving a complaint is a behavioural event, not just a procedural closure, within inclusive financial services. JEL Classification Codes: G21, G41, D18, D91, M31.

latest.title: Brand Image Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Bauran Pemasaran dan Lifestyle Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian
latest.venue: Jurnal Akuntansi Ekonomi dan Manajemen Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of the marketing mix (product quality, price, and promotion) and lifestyle on purchasing decisions for Apple smartphones in Samarinda City, with brand image serving as a mediating variable. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, data were collected from 145 Apple smartphone users in Samarinda. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares (PLS). The findings indicate that product quality, promotion, and lifestyle have a positive and significant effect on brand image as well as on purchasing decisions, both directly and indirectly. However, price was found to have no significant effect on brand image. This finding suggests that Apple consumers in Samarinda perceive price as a logical consequence of a premium product rather than as a primary factor in shaping brand image. Therefore, strengthening the lifestyle ecosystem appears to be more effective than merely adjusting pricing strategies. Future research is recommended to expand the framework by incorporating additional variables in order to provide a deeper analysis of the factors driving consumer purchasing decisions.

latest.title: Contextual institutional constraints and gender entrepreneurship in rural contexts
latest.venue: International Journal of Entrepreneurial Behaviour & Research
latest.abstract: Purpose This study explores the dual influence of contextual institutional constraints and gender entrepreneurship in rural contexts. Gender is applied as a critical lens to theorise entrepreneurship and its constraints (Ghouse and McElwee, 2026) in the gendered context (Welter, 2020) of rural family businesses. Design/methodology/approach From a dataset capturing the life stories of 30 entrepreneurs engaged in 22 rural family businesses, this work applies a gender lens and focuses on the life stories of 4 couples (men and women) owning and managing family businesses in rural Sweden. Following Larty and Hamilton (2011), the analysis structures the narratives of entrepreneurs in rural family businesses (cf. Alkhaled and Berglund, 2018) with the emerging themes of emancipation, empowerment and family business as an emancipatory space emerging as significant recurring themes in the stories of all four couples. Findings The findings reveal that rural family businesses provide women with a secure space that empowers and emancipates them to pursue entrepreneurial activities. Fathers play an important role in how daughters challenge traditional rural social norms, while contextual informal institutional constraints (i.e. traditional norms) hinder entrepreneurship in rural contexts. Here, the community acts as a vital stakeholder. Research limitations/implications This study challenges the assumptions of the heroic entrepreneur and the taken-for-granted agency of men. As such, in rural contexts, men act as co-agents to women entrepreneurs in pursuing entrepreneurship and emancipation. By including the voices of both women and men, this study responds to calls by scholars in the gender entrepreneurship literature (Smith, 2022; Hytti et al., 2024). Though empirical context is lim

latest.title: Human or Not? Prior Knowledge, Recognition of Virtual Identity, and Neural and Subjective Responses to a Hyperrealistic Virtual Influencer
latest.abstract: Despite the growing popularity of virtual social media influencers (VIs), little is known about how knowledge and recognition of a VI's virtual identity are associated with neural and subjective responses. We investigated whether prior knowledge of virtual identity, recognition during viewing, or remaining unaware was associated with differences in brain activity and subjective evaluations. Twenty female college students viewed a 1-minute silent video featuring a hyperrealistic Korean virtual influencer while electroencephalographic (EEG) activity was recorded. Subsequently, participants completed subjective evaluations and retrospectively reported prior knowledge or recognition of the influencer's virtual identity. Exploratory analyses compared EEG changes from eyes-closed rest and five subjective evaluation composite scores across the three groups, with correction for multiple comparisons. After correction for multiple comparisons, neither the EEG analyses nor the subjective composite analyses yielded statistically significant group differences. Descriptive means varied across groups, but these imprecisely estimated patterns did not establish group differences. The findings underscore the methodological importance of distinguishing prior knowledge from recognition during viewing. Computers Are Social Actors and Uncanny Valley perspectives generate hypotheses for future time-resolved studies rather than mechanisms demonstrated by the present data.

latest.title: Pengalaman Pemulihan Psikologis setelah Mengalami Putus Hubungan Romantis
latest.venue: Karakter Jurnal Riset Ilmu Pendidikan Islam
latest.abstract: A romantic relationship breakup is a challenging interpersonal experience that triggers emotional shifts and requires gradual psychological adjustment. This study aimed to explore the psychological recovery experience following a breakup, focusing on initial psychological conditions, coping strategies, supporting and inhibiting factors, and attributed meanings. Using a descriptive qualitative design, this study involved four undergraduate students at Universitas Muhammadiyah Aceh (aged 20–22 years; former relationship duration 1–3 years; 3–10 months post-breakup). Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews, non-verbal observations, and document analysis. The data were interactively analyzed using data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification. Findings revealed that all four participants experienced negative emotional responses initially, including sadness, disappointment, emptiness, and self-blame. The recovery process was achieved through acceptance, restricting communication with ex-partners, engaging in academic activities and hobbies, and seeking support from family and close friends. Key barriers included lingering memories, nostalgia, and shared routines. Ultimately, participants interpreted the breakup as a catalyst for self-acceptance, independence, personal boundaries, and readiness for healthier future relationships. Psychological recovery proved to be a personal, non-linear, and dynamic process.

latest.title: From Vision to Performance: The Mediating Role of Organizational Culture in an Explanatory Sequential Mixed Methods Study
latest.abstract: This study examines how vision and mission internalization influences employee performance through the mediating role of organizational culture at PT Solusi Bangun Indonesia Tbk Tuban Plant. An explanatory sequential mixed methods design was employed. Quantitative data were collected from 150 employees using structured questionnaires and analyzed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), followed by thematic analysis of in-depth interviews to explain the quantitative findings. The results reveal that vision and mission internalization significantly strengthens organizational culture, while organizational culture significantly improves employee performance. However, the direct effect of vision and mission internalization on employee performance is not significant, indicating that organizational culture functions as a full mediator. Qualitative findings demonstrate that leadership role modeling, continuous communication, and the institutionalization of organizational values into daily work practices are the primary mechanisms through which strategic values become productive employee behaviors. These findings highlight that organizations should prioritize cultivating a strong organizational culture rather than relying solely on communicating strategic statements. This study is limited to a single manufacturing company, which may restrict the generalizability of the findings to other organizational and industrial contexts.

latest.title: You are a part of me? Mother’s self-boundary blurring is associated with risk of the child’s mental health problems
latest.abstract: Abstract Mother plays a critical role in child’s mental health, with mother’s characteristics—such as cognitions, emotions, and behaviors—significantly influencing child’s development. Notably, these features are closely intertwined with mother’s self-concept. However, the relationship between mother’s self-concept and child’s mental health remains unclear. The present study investigated whether and how mother’s self-boundary blurring (i.e., over-permeability of the boundary between self and child) is associated with child’s mental health. Study 1 employed a questionnaire survey with 274 mother-youth dyads, and Study 2 used a cognitive-behavioral experiment with 46 mother-youth dyads. The results showed that mother’s self-boundary blurring was positively associated with youth’s depressive tendency via mother’s psychological control. These findings highlight the association between mother’s self-concept and child’s mental health problems, providing a new perspective for family interventions.
