latest.title: Enhancing Electric Scooter Reliability: An Assessment of Product Defects and After-Sales Service Quality
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Abhijith VR, Shijoy Shibu, Abeen Binoji, Arjun Sujith, Abhijith M, Vignesh V, Roshin T V
latest.abstract: Electric-scooter quality assessment requires separating reported symptoms, verified component failures and failures of service recovery. This study examines the Ola Electric case through a structured secondary-data assessment of complaint aggregates, company disclosures and an illustrative eleven-family defect taxonomy. A company filing confirms 10,644 complaints associated with a 2024 consumer-protection notice. Contemporaneously reported counts for service delay, delivery delay and unfulfilled service promises total 6,747, or 63.39% of that total. These categories indicate fulfilment and recovery concerns; they do not measure fleet failure incidence. An audit of assumed defect weights yields a 58% hardware and 42% software/electronic allocation, with 63% assigned to five families and 85% to eight. These are scenario properties rather than observed defect frequencies. Company-reported service turnaround and satisfaction measures provide contextual recovery indicators but cannot establish a causal restoration of trust. The principal contribution is an evidence-disciplined prioritisation framework that combines complaint burden, safety review and verified failure diagnosis. A proposed corrective-action process links vehicle-level events, repair records and post-repair recurrence. The analysis supports an integrated product-and-service quality agenda while identifying the operational data needed to validate it.

latest.title: From incidents to outcomes: consumer reactions and firm responses to negative environmental and social practices
Social Commerce Adoption and MSME Marketing Performance: The Mediating Role of Digital Trust and the Moderating Role of Digital Literacy
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh adopsi social commerce terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM melalui peran mediasi kepercayaan digital, serta menguji peran moderasi literasi digital pada hubungan antara adopsi social commerce dan kepercayaan digital. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan populasi UMKM sektor kuliner, fesyen, dan kerajinan di Kota Surakarta yang telah mengadopsi social commerce. Sampel ditentukan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling dengan jumlah 150 responden UMKM. Data dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) melalui perangkat lunak SmartPLS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa adopsi social commerce berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM maupun terhadap kepercayaan digital, kepercayaan digital berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM, serta kepercayaan digital terbukti memediasi secara parsial pengaruh adopsi social commerce terhadap kinerja pemasaran UMKM. Namun, literasi digital tidak terbukti memoderasi pengaruh adopsi social commerce terhadap kepercayaan digital. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi teoritis melalui penerapan kerangka Stimulus-Organism-Response pada konteks transformasi digital UMKM, serta implikasi praktis bahwa penguatan kepercayaan digital merupakan strategi kunci bagi UMKM dalam mengoptimalkan manfaat social commerce, sementara literasi digital lebih berperan sebagai prediktor langsung dibandingkan faktor penguat.

latest.title: Modal Ventura Syariah sebagai Alternatif Permodalan Bagi UKM di Indonesia dan Perbandingan Dengan Malaysia
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran Modal Ventura Syariah sebagai alternatif sumber permodalan bagi Usaha Kecil dan Menengah (UKM) di Indonesia, khususnya melalui kajian terhadap kerangka regulasi, mekanisme operasional, pengelolaan risiko, serta perbandingannya dengan Malaysia. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan jenis penelitian kepustakaan (library research) dan pendekatan deskriptif-komparatif. Data diperoleh dari peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK), fatwa Dewan Syariah Nasional Majelis Ulama Indonesia (DSN-MUI), artikel jurnal ilmiah, buku, serta dokumen resmi yang relevan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Modal Ventura Syariah memiliki potensi untuk menjadi alternatif pembiayaan UKM melalui skema penyertaan modal dan pembiayaan berbasis bagi hasil dengan akad seperti mudharabah dan musyarakah. Penerapan prinsip tersebut juga terlihat pada PT PBMT Syariah yang tidak hanya memberikan pembiayaan, tetapi turut mendukung pengembangan usaha melalui pendampingan manajemen dan peningkatan kapasitas mitra. Meskipun demikian, pengembangan Modal Ventura Syariah di Indonesia masih menghadapi sejumlah kendala, antara lain keterbatasan permodalan, rendahnya literasi keuangan syariah, risiko pembiayaan, serta tantangan dalam menjaga kepatuhan terhadap prinsip syariah. Sementara itu, Malaysia menunjukkan penguatan kelembagaan melalui keterlibatan penasihat syariah dalam keputusan investasi dan dukungan pendanaan dari pemerintah. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa pengembangan Modal Ventura Syariah di Indonesia memerlukan penguatan regulasi, tata kelola kelembagaan, pengawasan syariah, dan dukungan permodalan agar mampu meningkatkan akses pembiayaan serta mendorong pertumbuhan UKM secara berkelanjutan.

latest.title: The Role of Customer Satisfaction In Mediating The Effect of Service Performance and Perceived Value On Customer Loyalty: Evidence From A B2B Outsourced Cleaning Service In A Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Setting
latest.venue: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Outsourced facility services have become a strategic component of operations in Indonesia's highly regulated pharmaceutical industry, where cleanliness is not a cosmetic concern but a compliance requirement embedded in CPOB, WHO Prequalification, ISO 9001:2015, and ISO 14001:2015 standards. This study examined why an outsourced cleaning-service provider operating exclusively for a single pharmaceutical client since 2013 recorded 38 client complaints between November 2025 and January 2026, of which 66% concerned Service Performance and Perceived Value, and asked whether Customer Satisfaction mediates the effects of these two constructs on Customer Loyalty. Prior research has largely tested this chain in consumer-facing settings, leaving the business-to-business, compliance-driven pharmaceutical outsourcing context empirically unexamined. A quantitative, explanatory cross-sectional survey collected primary data from 355 employees of PT Bio Farma (Persero) Pasteur, Bandung, drawn by simple random sampling from a population of 3,096 and analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS. All eight hypotheses were supported at the 5% significance level. The model explained 74.0% of the variance in Customer Satisfaction and 68.3% of the variance in Customer Loyalty. Service Performance showed the strongest association with Customer Satisfaction (β = 0.543; f² = 0.901), while Customer Satisfaction showed the strongest association with Customer Loyalty (β = 0.494) and partially mediated both upstream paths (indirect effects β = 0.269 and β = 0.229). The study empirically extends the satisfaction-mediation framework to regulated B2B outsourcing and indicates that satisfaction management should be the central lever in loyalty-building strategy.

latest.title: The Influence of Profitability, Interest Rates (BI Rate) and Institutional Ownership on Stock Returns at PT Akasha Wira Internasional Tbk
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationships between profitability, the Bank Indonesia policy interest rate, institutional ownership, and stock returns at PT Akasha Wira International Tbk over the 2013–2024 period. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data obtained from the company’s annual reports and Bank Indonesia publications. The dataset comprises 12 annual observations. Profitability was measured using return on assets (ROA), while institutional ownership was measured by the proportion of shares held by institutional investors. The interest-rate variable was based on Bank Indonesia’s published policy-rate series, taking into account changes in the official benchmark terminology during the observation period. Multiple linear regression and hypothesis testing were conducted using SPSS version 23. The results indicate that profitability is positively and significantly associated with stock returns (t = 4.476, p = 0.002), whereas the policy interest rate is negatively and significantly associated with stock returns (t = −2.830, p = 0.022). Institutional ownership does not exhibit a statistically significant partial association with stock returns (t = 1.803, p = 0.109). Simultaneously, the three independent variables are statistically significant in the regression model (F = 10.610, p = 0.004). The model yields an R-squared of 0.799, indicating that the predictors jointly account for 79.9% of the in-sample variation in stock returns, while the adjusted R-squared is 0.724 after accounting for the number of predictors and observations. Given the limited sample and single-company setting, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. This study provides case-specific evidence concerning the relationships between firm-level profitability, monetary policy, owner

latest.title: The Effect of Campus Image and Word of Mouth on Students' Decisions in Choosing a Business Education Study Program at State University Of Medan
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi, Manajemen dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of campus image and word of mouth on the decision of 2025 cohort students in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Universitas Negeri Medan. This research employed a quantitative approach using an ex post facto method. The population consisted of 111 students, all of whom were selected as the sample through the total sampling technique. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, and the coefficient of determination (R²). The results showed that campus image had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (t value = 7.322; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Word of mouth also had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (t value = 5.779; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Simultaneously, both variables had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (f value = 40.939; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). The findings indicate that 43.1% of the variation in students' decisions to choose the Business Education Study Program can be explained by campus image and word of mouth, while the remaining 56.9% is influenced by other factors outside the scope of this study.

latest.title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
latest.venue: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Economy and Management Study
latest.abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

latest.title: Perceived constraints to air travel for people with chronic health conditions
latest.venue: Consumer Behavior in Tourism and Hospitality
latest.abstract: Purpose Chronic health conditions are conditions that persist for at least one year, require ongoing medical attention and affect daily life. The purpose of this exploratory study is to obtain insight into the perceived constraints to traveling economy class via commercial air carriers for American adults living with chronic health conditions to better understand the travel behavior of this understudied subset of consumers. Design/methodology/approach This paper uses a phenomenological, qualitative approach. In-depth interviews were conducted with 14 middle-class American adults with chronic conditions characterized by fatigue, pain and/or mobility issues and travel for work and/or leisure. Inductive thematic analysis was used to understand subjective meanings associated with lived experiences. Findings Based on experiences, participants perceived significant intrapersonal constraints, both physical and psychological, to traveling via commercial air. Participants also identified interpersonal and structural constraints, and the potential for these constraints fed back into intrapersonal constraints. Originality/value Although academic research on tourism and disabilities has gained traction in recent years, the literature has neglected to adequately investigate the needs, experiences and behaviors of travelers with chronic health conditions. This paper answers Zientara’s (2026) call for expanded ideas of disability and accessibility as well as greater qualitative research to understand the lived experiences of these travelers.

latest.title: Bank complaint resolution outcomes and customer behavioural biases for accountable financial institutions in guwahati India
latest.venue: International Journal of Marketing Research Innovation
latest.abstract: Customer complaints against banks in India have risen sharply with the spread of digital banking, and accountable and transparent grievance redressal has become central to consumer protection and strong institutions. Earlier studies linked complaint handling to satisfaction and loyalty but paid little attention to how the outcome of a resolved complaint shapes the customer's later judgement. This study examines the influence of bank complaint resolution outcomes on four post-resolution behavioural biases: confirmation bias, loss aversion, overconfidence and complaint avoidance. Primary data were collected through a cross-sectional survey using a structured questionnaire from 547 customers across 329 branches of 12 public- and 12 private-sector banks in Guwahati City, India, who had lodged a formal complaint and were analysed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha and simple linear regression. The results show that 56.3% of complaints were fully resolved, 40.0% partially resolved, and 3.7% not resolved, and that the bias scales were reliable (α = 0.781 to 0.893). Complaint resolution outcome was positively related to confirmation bias (β = 0.764, R² = 0.584), loss aversion (β = 0.808, R² = 0.652) and overconfidence (β = 0.663, R² = 0.440), and negatively related to complaint avoidance (β = −0.783, R² = 0.613), all at p < 0.001. Loss aversion recorded the highest mean score (3.88) and confirmation bias the lowest (2.68). The findings suggest that complaint resolution outcomes account for 44.0% to 65.2% of the variation in post-resolution behavioural biases, indicating that resolving a complaint is a behavioural event, not just a procedural closure, within inclusive financial services. JEL Classification Codes: G21, G41, D18, D91, M31.

latest.title: Brand Image Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Bauran Pemasaran dan Lifestyle Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian
latest.venue: Jurnal Akuntansi Ekonomi dan Manajemen Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of the marketing mix (product quality, price, and promotion) and lifestyle on purchasing decisions for Apple smartphones in Samarinda City, with brand image serving as a mediating variable. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, data were collected from 145 Apple smartphone users in Samarinda. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares (PLS). The findings indicate that product quality, promotion, and lifestyle have a positive and significant effect on brand image as well as on purchasing decisions, both directly and indirectly. However, price was found to have no significant effect on brand image. This finding suggests that Apple consumers in Samarinda perceive price as a logical consequence of a premium product rather than as a primary factor in shaping brand image. Therefore, strengthening the lifestyle ecosystem appears to be more effective than merely adjusting pricing strategies. Future research is recommended to expand the framework by incorporating additional variables in order to provide a deeper analysis of the factors driving consumer purchasing decisions.

latest.title: Fear of Missing Out and Hyperconnectivity: An Empirical Economic Study on African SMEs
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Abstract: This article examines the role of Fear of Missing Out (FOMO) as a growth lever for African SMEs. Using ANSD data and sectoral reports, a multiple linear regression model integrates five variables: digitalization, AI adoption and penetration, Internet connectivity, and social media usage. Results show that internet (53.9%) and social media (28.8%) together explain over 80% of FOMO intensity, highlighting their central role in impulsive consumer behavior. Digitalization contributes secondarily, while AI remains marginal yet strategic. A comparison across Senegal, Nigeria, Kenya, and Ghana reveals a pan-African dynamic. Keywords: FOMO, Consumer, Supply Analysis, Modern Marketing, Risk JEL Classification Number: D3, D11, M31, G32

latest.title: Due Diligence in Agribusiness, Natural Resource Governance, and Trade: Rethinking Voluntary Standards Under Sustainability Regulations
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines how sustainability due diligence is reshaping market access, private governance, and natural resource governance in agri‐food supply chains. It focuses on the EU Regulation on Deforestation‐Free Products (EUDR), which conditions market access on traceability and plot‐level geolocation, and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CS3D), which strengthens firm‐level obligations to identify and manage environmental and human rights risks across value chains. The study draws on qualitative analysis of WTO Technical Barriers to Trade Committee discussions and 64 interviews with producers, cooperatives, exporters, NGOs, and public officials in Costa Rica's coffee and palm oil sectors. Findings highlight that due diligence requirements reallocate evidentiary responsibilities and associated costs upstream, where participation increasingly depends on digital infrastructure, administrative capacity, and access to finance. Voluntary Sustainability Standards remain relevant as a business‐to‐business language of sustainability and may continue to provide consumer‐facing information, but they are being repositioned as auxiliary tools for risk documentation. The article asserts that sustainability markets are moving toward a new generation of criteria rooted in risk‐based traceability, documented environmental and social production conditions, and credible evidence of risk management. These dynamics risk creating “passporting” effects, whereby evidentiary capacity becomes a condition for market participation, with uneven consequences for producers, suppliers, and natural resource governance.

latest.title: Penagihan Pinjaman Online dalam Hukum Ekonomi Syariah: Rekonstruksi Berbasis Trilogi Ajaran Islam
latest.venue: Eksekusi Jurnal Ilmu Hukum dan Administrasi Negara
latest.abstract: The development of online lending through technology-based peer-to-peer financing services has expanded public access to financing, yet it has also raised ethical concerns in debt collection practices, particularly regarding intimidation, psychological pressure, misuse of personal data, and actions that undermine debtor dignity. This study aims to analyze the ethics of online loan collection from the perspective of Islamic economic law and to formulate a reconstruction based on the trilogy of Islamic teachings: aqidah, sharia, and akhlaq. This research employs a literature-based approach using an integrative-narrative review and conceptual paper design through the synthesis of regulations, fatwas, Islamic economic law literature, maqashid al-shariah, consumer protection, and fintech lending studies. The findings indicate that online loan collection should not be assessed solely based on platform legality or contract validity, but also through the principles of justice, trustworthiness, wealth protection, personal data protection, and respect for human dignity. Aqidah functions as the foundation of transcendental awareness, sharia as the normative boundary of transactions, and akhlaq as the ethical standard in exercising debt collection rights. This study contributes an integrative ethical framework for strengthening sharia fintech governance, ensuring that debt collection practices are not only legally compliant but also fair, humane, and oriented toward public welfare.

latest.title: A Study on the Impact of Green Marketing on Consumer Buying Behaviour with Special Reference to Chennai City
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Environmental degradation and climate change have compelled businesses to integrate ecological sustainability into their core marketing strategies. This study examines the impact of green marketing practices on consumer buying behaviour among urban consumers in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. A structured questionnaire was administered to a sample of 110 respondents across North, Central, South, and West Chennai using convenience and purposive sampling techniques. Primary data were analyzed using percentage analysis, One-Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), Pearson Chi-Square test of independence, and Henry Garrett Ranking technique. The One-Way ANOVA reveals a statistically significant difference in green buying behaviour across monthly income groups (F = 32.804, p < 0.001), confirming that higher-income consumers exhibit stronger eco-friendly purchasing tendencies. The Chi-Square analysis establishes a significant association between consumer awareness of green marketing and frequency of green product purchases (Chi-Square = 19.632, p = 0.0006). Furthermore, Henry Garrett Ranking identifies environmental concern and sustainability (mean score = 57.39) as the foremost driver of green purchases, followed by eco-friendly packaging and health benefits. The findings offer actionable insights for marketers and policymakers to strengthen green brand credibility and affordability in metropolitan markets.

latest.title: A Case Study on the Corporate Social Responsibility Initiatives of Tata Group from the perspective of Established CSR Models and Sustainability
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
authors: Ms. Khushbu Sahu and Dr. Navneet Kaur Bhatia
latest.abstract: This research aims to identify and analyze the implementation of Corporate Social Responsibility activities by the multinational corporation Tata group, which is the oldest and biggest group leading in steel, automobiles, IT services, telecommunications, hospitality and consumer products. The concept of CSR emerged from the growing recognition that businesses have more responsibilities towards society and environment beyond just earning profit. The implementation of CSR activities is crucial for the company as company need to balance economic, social and environmental goals together as it cannot function separately. Qualitative method and CSR models have been used for analysis. Research found that Tata Group carries many activities including philanthropic, social, environmental, ethical and legal responsibility. This research explored, Tata Group exemplifies how a corporation can integrate various CSR frameworks including Carroll’s ethical, philanthropic and legal responsibilities, the Triple Bottom Line’s sustainability. The implementation of CSR by Tata Group from the perspective of the models and sustainability has a significant impact on growth of the company and can positively influence its business expansion and strength

latest.title: Purchasing Behaviour and Consumer Perceptions of Quick-commerce Platforms for Dairy and Food Products in Anand and Ahmedabad, India
latest.venue: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports
latest.abstract: Quick commerce enables app-based ordering and rapid delivery of groceries, including perishable foods. This descriptive cross-sectional study examines self-reported purchasing behaviour and perceptions among 200 web-survey respondents in Anand and Ahmedabad, Gujarat (100 per city), surveyed in July 2026. Aggregate frequencies were converted to percentages using 200 as the denominator. Platform A was the most frequently used quick-commerce platform (56.0%), followed by Platform B (26.5%), Platform C (14.5%) and Platform D (3.0%). Packaged foods and snacks (79.5%), milk (29.0%), curd/yoghurt (17.0%) and paneer, butter or cheese (10.5%) were among the selected product categories. Emergency or last-minute requirements (29.0%) and convenience or time savings (27.0%) were the leading stated reasons for choosing quick commerce. Although 57.5% retrospectively reported increased purchase frequency, only 29.5% reported increased monthly expenditure. Positive responses were recorded for perceived time savings (78.0%) and overall experience meeting expectations (72.5%). Poor freshness or quality (26.5%) and short remaining shelf life (23.0%) were the most frequently identified problems; 48.0% were neutral regarding shelf-life suitability and handling. Continued purchasing was anticipated by 52.0%, whereas 42.0% were uncertain. These results describe the reported experiences of a geographically limited web-survey sample and do not establish causal effects or population-level estimates.

latest.title: Olok-Olok di Kolom Komentar TikTok: Tanggapan Warganet atas Musibah Mobil Listrik dan Mobil China
latest.abstract: News of vehicle incidents abroad now reaches Indonesian audiences through the TikTok accounts of national news outlets, turning comment sections into sites of public interpretation that are rarely studied as expressions of consumer responses to foreign brands. This exploratory study examines the themes in comments on news of incidents involving electric and Chinese-made cars outside Indonesia, how likes are distributed across those themes, and whether themes differ by comment layer and incident type. A content analysis with an inductive codebook was applied to comments on 17 purposively selected videos from Indonesian news and automotive accounts. A total of 3,629 Indonesian-language comments were coded into eleven non-exclusive themes by a large language model; reliability was tested with an independent human coder on 200 comments (mean kappa 0.75). Mockery and humor were the largest substantive theme (22.5%). It received 83.4% of likes, but its median was zero and ten comments accounted for most of its likes. Top-level comments contained more humor, safety concerns and purchase refusal, whereas replies contained more brand loyalty, defense and off-topic exchanges. Differences by incident type were descriptive and not robust when tested across videos. Comment sections in this corpus appear as layered conversations with highly concentrated attention, so likes should not be read as broad endorsement. The findings do not represent Indonesian netizens in general.

Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa media sosial yang digunakan dalam kegiatan promosi adalah TikTok dan Instagram karena banyak digunakan oleh masyarakat dan dapat membantu memperluas jangkauan promosi. Dalam merespons pelanggan, kritik dan saran digunakan sebagai bahan evaluasi untuk memperbaiki kualitas produk. Media sosial juga memberikan manfaat terhadap penjualan karena membantu konsumen mengenal produk, terutama ketika produk menjadi viral atau ramai dibicarakan. latest.title: Beyond the Click: How Brand Familiarity Bridges and Amplifies the Relationship Between Online Customer Experience and Shopping Behavior Across Three Asian Markets
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of online customer experience on online shopping behavior and investigates the dual role of brand familiarity as both a mediating mechanism and a moderating condition across Pakistan, China, and Bangladesh.Data came from a cross-sectional survey of 887 online consumers from Pakistan (n = 308), China (n = 292), and Bangladesh (n = 287). Grounded in the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework, the analysis used SPSS 28 and Hayes’ PROCESS macro: regression, bootstrapped mediation (Model 4), moderation (Model 1), and one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc tests.Online customer experience was positively associated with online shopping behavior (β = 0.60, p < 0.001) and brand familiarity (β = 0.57, p < 0.001). Brand familiarity was positively associated with online shopping behavior (β = 0.41, p < 0.001), partially mediating the relationship between online customer experience and online shopping behavior (indirect effect β = 0.23, 95% CI [0.15, 0.32]). Brand familiarity also strengthened this relationship (interaction β = 0.12, p < 0.001). Cross-country comparisons revealed significantly higher levels of all three constructs in China than in Pakistan and Bangladesh.This study extends the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework by examining brand familiarity as an organismic state with two roles. It investigates whether brand familiarity mediates the relationship between online customer experience and shopping behavior and whether it strengthens that relationship. By examining these mechanisms in three Asian e-commerce markets at different stages of digital maturity, the study provides insight into how online experiences relate to shopping behavior. The findings also point to the value of combining high-quality online experiences with str

latest.title: Brand Image, e-WoM, and Hedonic Motivation in GTA V Purchase Decisions among Indonesian Generation Z
latest.abstract: more than a decade after its initial release, making it a useful legacy-game context for examining how brand perceptions, consumer-generated digital information, and enjoyment-related motives are associated with purchase decisions among Indonesian Generation Z consumers. Objective: This study examines the associations of brand image, electronic word of mouth (e-WoM), and hedonic motivation with GTA V purchase decisions among Generation Z in Indonesia. Methods: A cross-sectional quantitative survey was administered online to 250 respondents recruited through purposive sampling. The four constructs were measured with 16 indicators on a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS 26. Results: Brand image (B = 0.285, t = 4.215, p < 0.001), e-WoM (B = 0.312, t = 4.682, p < 0.001), and hedonic motivation (B = 0.364, t = 5.841, p < 0.001) were each positively associated with purchase decision. The model was significant (F = 130.421, p < 0.001) and explained 61.4% of the variance based on adjusted R². Conclusion: Purchase decisions for this legacy video game are statistically associated with brand-related perceptions, digital consumer communication, and hedonic motives. Because the reported coefficients are unstandardized and the design is cross-sectional, the findings do not establish relative dominance or causality.

latest.title: From Ancient Wisdom to Corporate Strategy: A Conceptual Framework Integrating Indian Knowledge Systems into Sustainable Human Capital and Consumer Engagement Practices
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: India is working toward Bharat@2047, a vision of a developed nation (Viksit Bharat) that must be economically competitive, ecologically responsible, and rooted in its own culture. The management ideas we use to get there matter. Current Human Resource Management (HRM) and marketing scholarship leans heavily on Western behavioral and transactional models. These models are analytically strong, but they tend to overlook indigenous ways of knowing that could build sustainability into an organisation's values instead of treating it as compliance. This conceptual paper turns to Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS), namely Vedantic philosophy, the Bhagavad Gita, Kautilya's Arthashastra, and the Buddhist-Jain ethical traditions. From these, it draws six constructs (Dharma, Karma Yoga, Triguna, Aparigraha, Seva and Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam) and links them to two applied areas of management: sustainable human capital development and consumer engagement. Building on literature from Indian management philosophy, sustainable HRM and ethical marketing, the paper proposes a "Dharmic Sustainability Model". In this model IKS constructs sit upstream as value-drivers that shape organisational practice. On the human capital side these practices cover recruitment, motivation, leadership and employee well-being. On the marketing side they cover trust-based branding, responsible-consumption messaging and community-centred engagement. Together they are expected to lead to triple-bottom-line outcomes that fit the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and India's development priorities for 2047. latest.title: Greenwashing In The Indian Textile Industry: Challeges And Sustainable Governance
latest.venue: HPNLU Journal of Environment & Disaster Management
latest.abstract: The textile and fashion industry have a significant importance to the economy and employment in India. This industry is continually under scrutiny due to its environmental impacts, including water pollution, high carbon emissions, and chemical waste. Many companies claim to adopt sustainable product practices in response to this surveillance. The textile and fashion industry have started claiming falsely that have led to new serious issue of Green washing – “the false marketing of products as sustainable and environmentally friendly without any substantive action to make them so”. The problem of Green washing in India by the textile industry will be examined thoroughly. This paper will examine misleading sustainable claims and their effect on consumers and environmental health. It will also analyse the legal framework addressing this issue. This paper will also recommend possible approaches, such as strengthening legal regulation, enforcing independent sustainability audits, and providing consumer access to combat the issue of green washing. India can become genuinely sustainable in the textile industry by ensuring transparency and accountability. There must be a balance between environmental responsibility and economic growth for a better future.

latest.title: Employer branding and decent work across industries comparing ITC Limited and ICICI Bank in India
latest.venue: International Journal of Marketing Research Innovation
latest.abstract: Competition for skilled talent has made employer branding a strategic lever for decent work, gender equality and sustainable organisational reputation, yet comparative evidence on how industry context shapes the employer value proposition remains scarce in India. The study examines how the employer branding practices communicated by ITC Limited, a fast-moving consumer goods conglomerate, and ICICI Bank, a private-sector bank, converge and differ. A qualitative multiple-case design was applied to secondary data centred on the 2024–25 reporting year and drawn from ten categories of public documents, including annual reports, Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reports, career portals and official LinkedIn content. Passages were coded against fourteen literature-derived themes, eight internal and six external, and compared across nine cross-case themes. The results show that all nine themes (100%) appear in both organisations; two (22%), diversity and inclusion and employee well-being, converge in content, while seven (78%) diverge in emphasis. ICICI Bank reports about 42,000 women employees (32% of its workforce), more than 10 million learning hours and around 10 learning days per employee, a digital academy covering five technology domains and a recruitment platform with three support channels. ITC Limited anchors its proposition in leadership development through the KITES internship programme and ranked among the top three finalists for best employer brand on LinkedIn among organisations with more than 10,000 employees. The findings suggest that employer branding themes are shared across industries, whereas the content of the employer value proposition and the digital channels that carry it are shaped by industry-specific talent requirements. latest.title: Decoding anthropomorphism: a multidimensional perspective on presence, parasocial relationship and purchase intention
latest.abstract: Abstract Virtual influencers have become an increasingly important marketing tool, yet existing research has offered limited insight into how their anthropomorphic attributes should be conceptualized and through which psychological mechanisms they influence consumer responses. Addressing this gap, this study conceptualizes virtual influencer anthropomorphism as a multidimensional construct consisting of physical anthropomorphism, interactivity intelligence, and mental human-likeness, and examines its effects on purchase intention through social presence, telepresence, and parasocial relationship. Using online survey data, the results show that all three anthropomorphic attributes positively enhance consumers’ social presence and telepresence, which in turn strengthen parasocial relationships and subsequently increase purchase intention. The findings further refine the conceptualization of virtual influencer anthropomorphism by highlighting the importance of interaction-based anthropomorphism alongside visual and mental human-like cues. Overall, this study contributes to the literature by clarifying both the multidimensional nature of virtual influencer anthropomorphism and the psychological process through which it shapes consumer behavior.

latest.title: Adoption-Stage-Based Content Strategy for Business-to-Business Industrial Marketing: A Case Study of an Indian Industrial Manufacturer's Business Development Product Portfolio
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Business-to-business (B2B) industrial organisations often possess strong engineering capability but limited structured marketing communication, which can leave genuinely useful products under-recognised by the very dealers and customers who already have access to them. This paper presents a case study of an applied content-strategy project carried out within the Business Development (BD) function of a large Indian industrial engine and power-generation manufacturer (referred to here as "the Company" for confidentiality), over an eight-week internship period. The study addresses three BD product portfolios – Product C (engine and genset maintenance offerings), Product B (a telematics and remote-monitoring device), and Product A (a pre-launch fuel additive) – for which no structured, stage-aware communication approach previously existed. Drawing on Rogers' Diffusion of Innovation theory, the Dynamic Staged Adoption Model, and literature on fear-of-missing-out (FOMO) driven consumer behaviour, the study develops and applies an integrated practitioner framework, termed the Who-How-What framework, which maps the customer's adoption category (Who), the product-adoption behaviour expected at each stage (How), and the communication trigger required to move the audience forward (What) across a five-gate adoption journey. Applying this framework across the three product portfolios resulted in 81 verified strategic marketing assets – 41 for Product A, 24 for Product C, and 16 for Product B – sequenced through stage-wise campaign calendars spanning 10 to 17 weeks per product, and distributed deliberately across LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Instagram, and owned channels according to the audience relevant at each stage. latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how the theory of consumption values (TCV), consumption motivations and emotions influence young consumers’ well-being perceptions, which subsequently shape brand love, brand respect and behavioral intentions toward halal farm-to-table (FTT) restaurants. It also compared same-ethnic and cross-ethnic Generation Z consumers to examine whether cultural background moderates the proposed relationships within this restaurant context. Design/methodology/approach This study used a quantitative research design by collecting data from 420 Generation Z consumers who had recently dined at halal FTT restaurants serving ethnic cuisine. Data were collected through on-site surveys at selected restaurant locations to ensure that respondents had a direct and recent dining experience for the study’s context. The data were subsequently analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings Economic value, consumption motivations and emotions were found to significantly enhance young consumers’ well-being perceptions, which in turn positively influenced brand love and brand respect. Importantly, well-being perception significantly influenced behavioral intentions indirectly through both brand love and brand respect, highlighting these brand-related mechanisms as important pathways linking well-being perceptions to behavioral intentions toward halal FTT restaurants. Both brand love and brand respect significantly strengthened behavioral intentions toward halal FTT restaurants. latest.title: Online search advertising under market uncertainty: consumer engagement, advertiser bidding, and cost efficiency
latest.abstract: This study examines how an external shock reshapes consumer and advertiser behavior in online search advertising markets. Using the COVID-19 pandemic as the empirical setting, we apply a difference-in-differences framework to keyword-level data from a leading South Korean search engine. We find that search ad impressions and clicks increased, while advertisers’ bids and cost-per-click (CPC) declined. These findings show that greater consumer exposure and engagement can coexist with lower click costs, consistent with more conservative bidding under uncertainty. Industry-level analyses reveal variations across industry sectors depending on demand urgency, risk relevance, online-channel reliance, and discretionary or deferrable demand. By examining consumer-side and advertiser-side outcomes together, this study extends the online advertising literature by showing how the two sides of an auction-based advertising market can respond differently to a common external shock, offering implications for managing search advertising under market uncertainty.

latest.title: PERSONALIZATION, PRIVACY AND TRUST IN AI-ASSISTED ONLINE SHOPPING: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK DISTINGUISHING TRUST IN THE ASSISTANT FROM TRUST IN THE RETAILER IN THE INDIAN CONTEXT
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Soumya Sanoj and Dr S. Alakendran
latest.abstract: Abstract AI-enabled shopping assistants now help consumers discover products, compare options and ask questions during online purchases. Whether shoppers act on that help depends on how relevant and how personal the advice feels, how well the assistant performs, and what shoppers believe is happening to their data. This conceptual paper develops a stimulus–organism–response framework for AI-assisted online shopping in India. It links two dimensions of perceived personalization (relevance and specificity) and chatbot quality to privacy concerns and trust, and through them to purchase intention. The paper makes three contributions. First, it separates trust in the assistant from trust in the retailer that deploys it. Second, it treats chatbot quality as a construct distinct from personalization and grounds it in research on AI chatbot service quality. Third, it brings together two roles of trust that earlier studies have specified separately, trust as a mediator and trust as a buffer against privacy concerns, in one model with a stated causal order and a route to testing. The framework draws on the technology acceptance model, trust research, privacy-calculus and privacy-boundary reasoning, and the computers-are-social-actors paradigm, and it is positioned against recent peer-reviewed studies of chatbots and shopping assistants, including studies of Indian shoppers. Eight propositions, boundary conditions, measurement guidance and an analytic strategy are offered for empirical work. India, where the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 are phasing in notice-and-consent duties, is a timely setting in which to test them. Keywords: AI shopping assistants; perceived personalization; chatbot quality; privacy concerns; consumer trust; purchase intention; personalization

latest.title: A Study of Regulatory Gaps and Consumer Protection in India's Rapidly Expanding BNPL Ecosystem
latest.abstract: Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) services have taken off quickly in the digital lending sector in India. Although they have made financial inclusion and access to credit more accessible, they also highlight some issues. This report looks at these issues with regard to BNPLs by looking at the lack of regulation, lack of clear pricing, aggressive collection processes and lack of credit bureau reporting. To understand the interaction between the new rules being introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and consumer protection, a mixed method approach was used. Population and Sample: The population consists of young working professionals and Undergraduates/Postgraduates who would be considered digitally active. There is a sample size of around 50-70 people to be included in the research. Data Sources: Primary data includes a questionnaire which will measure how aware people are of BNPL services, whether the service is transparent, what their spending habits are, how they repay and if they feel they have protections as a consumer. Secondary data includes notifications and directions from the RBI, peer reviewed literature, industry publications and financial reports. Data Collection: The information was collected through a questionnaire that contains closed and scaled questions to allow quantitative data to be collected. Some BNPL terms and conditions, pricing and credit documents were examined. This research demonstrates the need for standardised legislation, transparency and data protection. The findings suggest that there should be balance put into place to ensure that those most at risk of becoming over indebted are protected while promoting financial innovation in the digital credit sector in India.

latest.abstract: Digital platforms have expanded the ways in which food and dairy brands communicate product value, develop familiarity and reach geographically dispersed audiences. Yet, for many regional brands, the practical challenge is not simply selecting digital channels but coordinating creator acquisition, content production, product fulfilment and performance review as a connected process. This paper examines the operationalisation of influencer-led digital marketing at Desi Farms, a dairy brand of SNA Milk & Milk Products Pvt. Ltd., in Maharashtra, India, using an exploratory single-case study based on a two-month internship period (22 May–22 July 2026). Evidence comprised internship activity records, influencer coordination records, campaign-related work, publicly visible digital content and qualitative competitor observations. No consumer survey was conducted, and complete platform analytics, conversion data and verified sales outcomes were unavailable. The case records 76 influencer collaborations coordinated and 132 videos contributed against an initial target of 50 videos. Two short-duration Meta advertisements were used to attract potential creators; approximately 500–600 enquiries or responses were reported, of which around 100 suitable respondents were personally contacted. Four separate advertising strategies for product videos were prepared for management review but were not independently executed by the researcher. The findings describe a practical workflow linking creator screening, product-based barter negotiation, perishable-product delivery, content briefing, draft coordination and Instagram collaboration publication. latest.title: A atuação do sommelier de mel na valorização dos méis de abelhas nativas sem ferrão e de Apis mellifera na gastronomia
latest.abstract: This study analyzed the role of the honey sommelier in the valorization of honeys produced by stingless native bees and Apis mellifera in gastronomy. The qualitative, exploratory, and descriptive research was conducted through a literature review, questionnaires applied during guided tastings, and photographic records. The study included twelve participants, among them sommeliers, producers, chefs, and consumers. The results highlighted three central dimensions of the sommelier’s role: sensory, related to the identification of aromas, flavors, and textures; economic and market-related, linked to the repositioning of honey in higher value-added markets; and socio-environmental, associated with awareness of biodiversity and sustainability. The sommelier’s technical mediation was crucial for participants to recognize attributes often unnoticed in everyday consumption, as well as to promote gastronomic pairings and broaden knowledge about terroir and floral origin. It is concluded that the honey sommelier acts as a strategic agent at the intersection of gastronomy, culture, and sustainability, contributing to the sensory, cultural, and environmental valorization of Brazilian honeys.

How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Abstract Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: Abstract This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: Impact of digital transformation on SME’s marketing performance: role of social media and market turbulence
hot.abstract: Despite the rising relevance of digital transformation, there is still a knowledge vacuum due to limited literature available on digital transformation. This study aims to examine the impact of digital transformation on the marketing performance of small and medium enterprises. This research seeks to fill this void by adopting the technology adoption model in order to explore how in a fast-changing technological environment, digital transformation plays its role in firm specific capabilities that are imperative for a firm to adopt, and how they impact firm’s marketing performance. Combination of convenience sampling as well as snowball sampling was used to collect the data. Utilizing survey data from 316 small to medium-sized enterprises in the twin cities (Islamabad & Rawalpindi), Pakistan the results indicate that digital transformation has a positive influence on small and medium enterprises’ marketing performance. This encourages businesses to take advantage of the opportunity presented by new digital technologies and industry-wide digitalization trends by adopting new technologies and improving their digital capabilities in order to increase their productivity, efficiency, and innovation as well as their marketing performance. Hence this study is a practical demonstration of how developing digital transformation may be used to develop novel digital products and services and thereby improve marketing performance that leads to the overall corporate performance. Finally, the study contributes to the literature by evaluating the proposed model that describes the relationships between digital transformation, social media marketing, market turbulence and marketing performance concurrently.

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Theory and theory development: Guidelines for establishing theoretical gaps, foundations, contributions, and implications
hot.abstract: Theory guides the acquisition and advancement of knowledge. Despite its importance, developing and refining theories remains a formidable task, given the inadequate clarity, inherent confusion, and compounding complexity faced by scholars in theory development. In response, this article offers clear, coherent, and constructive guidelines to tackle these challenges in theory development. Adopting the 3 E s involving the author’s expertise , experience , and exposure , this guide offers a sequential approach to addressing theoretical gaps , theoretical foundations , theoretical contributions , and theoretical implications . This all-inclusive, accessible, and actionable resource seeks to benefit a diverse range of stakeholders, including both emerging and established scholars, which, in turn, contributes to ensuring the effective development of theories and, by extension, the return on value of these theories for funders, institutions, and, most importantly, the target beneficiaries (e.g., consumers, firms, society at large) of well-developed, theory-informed research.

hot.title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI's capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI's execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance.
