Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: What you see is not what you get: ESG scores and greenwashing risk
hot.abstract: This paper shows that ESG scores capture a company’s greenwashing behavior. Greenwashing accusations are most prevalent among large companies with high ESG scores. We empirically employ a novel theoretical model that distinguishes between the communication of a company’s environmental efforts (apparent environmental performance) and its actual environmental impact (real environmental performance). The correlation of the apparent (real) environmental performance with ESG scores is significantly positive (negative). Therefore, ESG scores are unsuitable for measuring real environmental impact. Thus, investors focusing on high ESG-rated companies may unknowingly increase their greenwashing risk exposure, and academics may use misleading information to assess greenwashing risk. • ESG scores are positively correlated with greenwashing cases. • ESG scores mainly measure the apparent rather than the real environmental performance. • Higher analyst coverage limits the exaggeration of apparent environmental performance.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: The impact of digital HRM system and digital transformation on HR efficiency with organizational agility as a moderator
hot.abstract: The study focuses on understanding the moderation effect of organizational agility in the impact of digital HRM system and digital transformation on HR efficiency in organizations intending to excel in the digital era. This study examines the association between digital HRM systems, digital transformation, and HR efficiency, considering the moderating role of organizational agility. Based on the study model, the authors proposed five hypotheses to be tested in this study. They adapted the study instrument based on quantitative descriptive approach and distributed 500 questioners to collect 385 responses. The study’s findings reveal that both digital HRM systems and digital transformation impact HR efficiency. The significant findings were that digital HRM systems (β = 0.456, p < 0.001) and digital transformation (β = 0.194, p = 0.006) have a positive and significant impact on HR efficiency. In addition, organizational agility serves as a moderator in the relationship between digital HRM systems and HR efficiency (β = 0.154, p = 0.025) but has no effect on the relationship with digital transformation (β = − 0.075, p = 0.248). This study contributes to the literature by demonstrating the role of digital HRM systems and digital transformation as key organizational resources that enhance HR efficiency. It also highlights how organizational agility and digital capabilities serve as dynamic resources, contributing to an organization’s adaptability and sustained competitive advantage. The future research directions and limitations are presented at the end.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The past, present, and future of sustainability marketing: How did we get here and where might we go?
hot.abstract: The ever-increasing concerns about global sustainability have sparked intense debates and actions across various sectors, with marketing playing a pivotal role in influencing both the problem and potential solutions. This article maps the historical trajectory of sustainability marketing, analyzes current trends, and explores future directions to enhance sustainability within marketing practice. We show that sustainability marketing has historically centered on resource conservation and green marketing , but in recent years its scope has expanded to encompass a broader range of topics. These include the circular economy , anti-consumption, regulatory frameworks, innovation, carbon emissions , as well as the social and ethical considerations inherent in sustainability marketing. We propose three main areas within which sustainability marketing might expand in the future: system-driven changes, business-driven changes, and consumer-driven changes. Our analysis aims to deepen the understanding of sustainability marketing and inspire marketers to explore questions and solutions that will contribute to a sustainable future.

hot.title: Greenwashing and market value of firms: An empirical study
hot.abstract: In today's business environment, green or sustainable claims are rising as companies strive to strengthen environmental practices in response to climate change and sustainable development challenges. However, with increasing expectations of sustainable performance, companies encounter mounting financial pressure to adopt more efficient sustainable practices, which may lead some to exploit sustainability efforts for their own gain. Many companies make environmentally friendly assertions to conceal or mask their actual activities—a phenomenon known as greenwashing—which fosters public scepticism about the authenticity of their green messaging. This study employs an event study methodology to examine how the stock market values greenwashing news, drawing on 121 global greenwashing news since the 2015 Paris Agreement. Our findings reveal a negative correlation between greenwashing news and stock market reactions. The market reactions to greenwashing news are more negative for firms with greater ESG performance than for weak ESG performance. Additionally, greenwashing news supported by concrete evidence elicits stronger adverse reactions. Companies operating in the manufacturing industry experience more significant market value losses than those in the service sector. The findings also indicate that the Asia-Pacific market demonstrates particularly strong negative responses to greenwashing news compared to other stock markets. This study contributes to the signalling theory and advances the literature on corporate sustainability practices by providing empirical insights in a global context.

hot.title: Digital literacy, digital accessibility, human capital, and entrepreneurial resilience: a case for dynamic business ecosystems
hot.abstract: This study examines the role of digital literacy, digital accessibility, and human capital in fostering entrepreneurial resilience among entrepreneurs in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These countries serve as exemplary models in digital transformation, particularly in navigating crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Grounded in the resource-based view and the theory of dynamic capabilities, this research investigates how these factors contribute to entrepreneurial resilience. This study employs structural equation modeling to analyze survey data from 317 individuals with entrepreneurial experience. According to the findings, digital literacy, accessibility, and human capital significantly enhance innovation, strengthening entrepreneurial resilience. Agility is identified as a key moderator, amplifying the positive impact of these competencies on resilience. Although the success of entrepreneurial ecosystems has often been attributed to entrepreneurial actors, resource providers, connectors, or entrepreneurial intentions, this study underscores the importance of fostering digital competencies and agility to build resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems. It offers policymakers and business leaders insights into the mechanisms that enhance resilience in dynamic and crisis-affected environments where the digital landscape is rapidly evolving.

hot.title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
hot.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies sparked a rapid development of smartphone applications designed to help individuals experiencing mental health problems through an AI-powered chatbot agent. However, the safety of such agents when dealing with individuals experiencing a mental health crisis, including suicidal crisis, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed the ability of 29 AI-powered chatbot agents to respond to simulated suicidal risk scenarios. Application repositories were searched and the app descriptions screened in search of apps that claimed to be beneficial when experiencing mental distress and offered an AI-powered chatbot function. All agents were tested with a standardized set of prompts based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale designed to simulate increasing suicidal risk. We assessed the responses according to pre-defined criteria based on the ability to provide emergency contact information and other factors. None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate. Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding. These findings raise concerns about the deployment of AI-powered chatbots in sensitive health contexts without proper clinical validation.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Social Media Marketing Strategies for Enhanced Customer Experience
hot.abstract: This paper explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in personalizing social media marketing strategies and its impact on customer experience, with a focus on consumers within the MENA region. Using data collected from an online questionnaire completed by 893 individuals, the study confirms that AI significantly enhances social media marketing by offering personalized content, optimizing influencer selection, and enabling real-time consumer interaction. These capabilities not only increase customer awareness but also improve user experience and purchase intentions. Key AI tools such as influencer marketing, content optimization, and customization are effective in capturing consumer attention, although further research is necessary to deepen understanding. By examining AI's ability to analyze vast datasets and support targeted marketing efforts, the study contributes to both academic and practical discourse, offering insights that businesses can use to refine their AI-driven social media strategies. Ultimately, the research aims to guide marketers through the complexities of AI deployment, ensuring its benefits are fully realized for consumers.

hot.title: Barriers and Enablers of AI Adoption in Human Resource Management: A Critical Analysis of Organizational and Technological Factors
hot.abstract: This paper examines the key factors recognized as transformative in the field of human resource management (HRM) and explores their influence on the global adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). While AI holds significant promise for enhancing HRM efficiency, employee engagement, and Decision Making, its implementation presents a range of organizational, technical, and ethical challenges that organizations worldwide must navigate. Change aversion, data security worries, and integration expenses are major roadblocks, but strong digital leadership, company culture, and advancements in NLP and machine learning are key enablers. This paper presents a complex analysis that questions the common perception of AI as only disruptive by delving into the relationship between power dynamics, corporate culture, and technology infrastructures. In this paper, we bring together research from several fields to help scholars and practitioners understand the nuances of AI adoption in HRM, with an emphasis on the importance of inclusive methods and ethical frameworks.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The Role of Digital Tourism Platforms in Advancing Sustainable Development Goals in the Industry 4.0 Era
hot.abstract: The intersection of digitalization and sustainability is reshaping the tourism industry, with digital platforms playing a transformative role in optimizing travel experiences while simultaneously influencing economic inclusivity, labor dynamics, and environmental responsibility. This paper explores how Industry 4.0 technologies—such as artificial intelligence (AI), big data, blockchain, virtual reality (VR), and the Internet of Things (IoT)—are integrated into digital tourism platforms, assessing their dual impact on sustainability and market structures. The study develops a conceptual framework around five key dimensions: market power and digital dependency, AI-driven automation and workforce transformation, innovation and digital inclusion, sustainability innovations, and data security and governance. While digital platforms enhance personalization, operational efficiency, and eco-conscious travel, they also reinforce economic disparities, monopolization, and regulatory challenges, raising concerns related to SDGs such as SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption, and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions). The study highlights the need for equitable governance frameworks to mitigate risks associated with AI-driven monopolization, algorithmic bias, and data privacy violations while ensuring digital accessibility for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on platform economics, digital governance, and sustainable tourism transformation, offering policy and managerial implications for fostering an inclusive and envi

hot.title: Economic, technological and environmental drivers of the circular economy in the European Union: a panel data analysis
hot.abstract: The circular economy has become a strategic priority in the European Union, aiming to reduce dependence on finite natural resources and promote a sustainable economic model. This study investigates the key factors influencing the use of circular materials in the European Union between 2010 and 2022, considering the impact of global challenges such as the coronavirus pandemic, the energy crisis, and geopolitical tensions. Unlike previous research, this study integrates economic, technological, and environmental dimensions, with a particular focus on the role of digital transformation as a catalyst for circularity. The research applies an econometric model based on the analysis of panel data to explore the interconnections between resource productivity, recycling rates, private sector investment, digitalization, and expenditures on research and development. The findings reveal a strong positive relationship between resource efficiency, recycling efforts, and the use of circular materials, emphasizing the importance of infrastructure and technological advancements in supporting circularity. However, significant regional differences among European Union member states are also identified, highlighting the need for targeted policies to address these disparities. In the context of European policies such as the Green Deal and the Circular Economy Action Plan, this study provides valuable insights for decision makers. The results suggest that increasing investment, expanding digital infrastructure, and fostering innovation are essential for accelerating the transition to a circular economy. This research contributes to the existing literature by offering a comprehensive perspective on circularity and demonstrating how digital transformation can enhance sustainability.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Hotel certifications are not only crucial for environmental sustainability, but also serve as

hot.title: A Comparison of Responses from Human Therapists and Large Language Model–Based Chatbots to Assess Therapeutic Communication: Mixed Methods Study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consumers are increasingly using large language model-based chatbots to seek mental health advice or intervention due to ease of access and limited availability of mental health professionals. However, their suitability and safety for mental health applications remain underexplored, particularly in comparison to professional therapeutic practices. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how general-purpose chatbots respond to mental health scenarios and compare their responses to those provided by licensed therapists. Specifically, we sought to identify chatbots' strengths and limitations, as well as the ethical and practical considerations necessary for their use in mental health care. METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study to compare responses from chatbots and licensed therapists to scripted mental health scenarios. We created 2 fictional scenarios and prompted 3 chatbots to create 6 interaction logs. We recruited 17 therapists and conducted study sessions that consisted of 3 activities. First, therapists responded to the 2 scenarios using a Qualtrics form. Second, therapists went through the 6 interaction logs using a think-aloud procedure to highlight their thoughts about the chatbots' responses. Finally, we conducted a semistructured interview to explore subjective opinions on the use of chatbots for supporting mental health. The study sessions were analyzed using thematic analysis. The interaction logs from chatbot and therapist responses were coded using the Multitheoretical List of Therapeutic Interventions codes and then compared to each other. RESULTS: We identified 7 themes describing the strengths and limitations of the chatbots as compared to therapists. These include elements of good therapy in chatbot responses, conversational style of c

hot.title: Strategic human resource management in the digital economy era: an empirical study of challenges and opportunities among MSMEs and startups in Indonesia
hot.abstract: This study investigates the impact of digital Human Resource Management (HRM) strategies on workforce productivity and organizational performance within Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and startups in Indonesia. Anchored in the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the research conceptualizes digital HRM as a strategic asset that enhances organizational performance by enabling firms to develop, deploy, and reconfigure human capital capabilities in response to digital transformation. The conceptual model includes five constructs: Digital Technology Adoption in HRM, Digital Training and Development, Work Flexibility and Hybrid Management, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention, and Utilization of HR Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Data were collected through structured questionnaires distributed to MSME and startup leaders and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with Smart PLS. The results indicate that Digital Technology Adoption, Digital Training and Development, and Work Flexibility do not significantly influence workforce productivity or organizational performance (p > 0.05). However, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention and the Utilization of HR Analytics and AI have a significant and positive impact on both workforce productivity and performance outcomes (p = 0.000). These findings highlight that while not all digital HR strategies yield immediate benefits, the ability to build dynamic capabilities through innovative talent practices and data-driven HR systems is essential to achieving competitive advantage and organizational success in the digital economy.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
latest.venue: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Economy and Management Study
latest.abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

latest.title: Brand Image, e-WoM, and Hedonic Motivation in GTA V Purchase Decisions among Indonesian Generation Z
latest.abstract: more than a decade after its initial release, making it a useful legacy-game context for examining how brand perceptions, consumer-generated digital information, and enjoyment-related motives are associated with purchase decisions among Indonesian Generation Z consumers. Objective: This study examines the associations of brand image, electronic word of mouth (e-WoM), and hedonic motivation with GTA V purchase decisions among Generation Z in Indonesia. Methods: A cross-sectional quantitative survey was administered online to 250 respondents recruited through purposive sampling. The four constructs were measured with 16 indicators on a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS 26. Results: Brand image (B = 0.285, t = 4.215, p < 0.001), e-WoM (B = 0.312, t = 4.682, p < 0.001), and hedonic motivation (B = 0.364, t = 5.841, p < 0.001) were each positively associated with purchase decision. The model was significant (F = 130.421, p < 0.001) and explained 61.4% of the variance based on adjusted R². Conclusion: Purchase decisions for this legacy video game are statistically associated with brand-related perceptions, digital consumer communication, and hedonic motives. Because the reported coefficients are unstandardized and the design is cross-sectional, the findings do not establish relative dominance or causality.

latest.title: Brand resilience under environmental threat: competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern in seafood purchase intentions
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how brand image shapes seafood purchase intentions under environmental threat. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework, it examines the competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern. Design/methodology/approach Using a systematic sampling approach, this study collected 319 valid questionnaires from coastal consumers in Guangdong Province, China. Structural equation modeling was used to test the dual-mediation model involving perceived value and environmental concern. Findings Brand image positively influences both perceived value and environmental concern. Perceived value enhances purchase intention, while environmental concern suppresses it. Both variables significantly mediate the brand–purchase relationship in opposing directions, with an overall positive indirect effect, suggesting that brand resilience endures despite ecological concerns. Originality/value This study contributes by modeling competing psychological mediators in seafood consumption under environmental threat, an area that has received limited attention in existing literature. It reveals consumer ambivalence during ecological crises: while strong brands retain appeal, environmental risk awareness weakens purchasing confidence. The findings offer actionable insights for seafood marketers on sustaining brand resilience through value communication and transparent sustainability practices.

latest.title: Transparency matters
latest.abstract: This study examines how sponsorship disclosure format and influencer compensation nature shape perceived sponsorship transparency and its effects on source credibility, information credibility, online engagement, and purchase intention among Instagram micro-influencers. Drawing on the Persuasion Knowledge Model, Communication Transparency Theory, Parasocial Interaction Theory, and Source Credibility Theory, the study conceptualizes perceived sponsorship transparency as consumers’ holistic judgment of how openly the commercial relationship is communicated. A between-subjects experiment (420 participants) was analyzed using two-way analysis of variance, regression, and serial mediation. Disclosure format, but not compensation nature, influenced perceived transparency, with platform-integrated disclosures outperforming hashtag-based ones, extending the Persuasion Knowledge Model to platform-governed ecosystems. Transparency sequentially mediated behavioral outcomes through source and information credibility, with source credibility the stronger mediator. Limitations include snowball sampling, a fictitious influencer and brand, and no confirmatory factor analysis.

latest.title: Role of corporate social responsibility in brand loyalty, emotional attachment and online behavior among Generation Z consumers: a cross-national study
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on the triple bottom line (TBL) framework and social identity theory (SIT), this study aims to examine how Generation Z consumers’ perceptions of the economic, environmental and social dimensions of corporate social responsibility (CSR) relate to brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, and how these relationships extend to electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) and online brand-related activities across national contexts. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 815 Generation Z consumers in Chile, Germany, Austria and Greece. Structural equation modeling was used to examine relationships among the three CSR dimensions and brand loyalty, emotional brand attachment, eWOM and online brand-related activities. Multi-group analysis was conducted to assess cross-national differences. Findings Environmental and economic CSR are positively associated with brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, whereas social CSR is negatively associated with brand loyalty and has no significant effect on emotional brand attachment. Brand loyalty positively influences eWOM, while emotional brand attachment positively influences online brand-related activities. Most structural relationships vary significantly across countries, although the relationship between emotional brand attachment and online brand-related activities remains consistent across countries. Originality/value The study advances CSR research by treating CSR as a multidimensional set of signals rather than a homogeneous construct and examining their differentiated implications for consumer–brand relationships. Integrating TBL with an identity-based perspective from SIT, it shows that different CSR dimensions may carry different relevance for Gen Z consumers, and that their effects vary across natio

latest.title: Modeling the Brand Strength Component in Monetary Brand Valuation Using Fuzzy Logic: Evidence From a Place Brand
latest.abstract: Abstract Purpose : Monetary brand valuation remains a persistent challenge in brand management, due to the absence of transparent approaches for operationalizing brand strength. While financial-based valuation methods are well established, the integration of perceptual and behavioral dimensions into monetary frameworks remains limited. The purpose of this study is to develop and test a methodological approach for modeling the Brand Strength component within monetary brand valuation. The approach is operationalized as an interpretable fuzzy inference model that integrates perceptual data, objective indicators, and expert knowledge. The case of Ülemiste City in Tallinn, Estonia, is used as an empirical example to demonstrate and test the approach’s practical applicability. Design/methodology/approach : The study proposes a fuzzy framework for estimating brand strength in monetary brand valuation. The approach integrates heterogeneous data sources, including survey-based perceptions, objective indicators, and expert knowledge, within a rule-based, interpretable model. The model is empirically demonstrated through an application to the Ülemiste City place brand. Findings : The results show that this model produces consistent, interpretable brand-strength coefficients and supports two complementary use cases: internal, target-based brand management and cross-brand comparability. The findings demonstrate that fuzzy logic provides a practical mechanism for combining diverse sources of brand-related information into a coherent monetary valuation framework. Originality/value : This study advances brand management by offering a transparent method for integrating brand strength into monetary valuation, linking financial metrics with perception-based assessments. Given the lack of

latest.title: When Does Sustainable Storytelling Foster Advocacy Intention? The Mediating Roles of Perceived ESG Authenticity and Emotional Brand Resonance, and the Moderating Role of Green Scepticism in Digital Ecosystems
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Amid widespread greenwashing and consumer scepticism, brands struggle to convert sustainability commitments into advocacy intention. This study examines sustainable digital storytelling encompassing narrative environmental framing (NEF), interactive sustainability co‐narration (ISC), and temporal impact visualisation (TIV) as a distinct communicative mode. Drawing on narrative transportation, signalling, and attribution theories, we develop a moderated‐mediation model linking these storytelling dimensions to sustainable consumption advocacy intention (SCAI) through perceived ESG authenticity (ESGA) and emotional brand resonance (EBR), with green scepticism (GSCP) as a boundary condition. A three‐wave, time‐lagged survey of 512 Vietnamese consumers confirms that all three storytelling dimensions enhance ESGA and EBR, which in turn predict advocacy intention, with no statistically significant residual direct effects of storytelling on advocacy. However, green scepticism attenuates these effects, diminishing compelling narratives' motivational impact. This study extends narrative transportation theory to the sustainable digital branding domain, identifies a dual cognitive‐affective pathway through which storytelling generates advocacy intention, and establishes green scepticism as a boundary condition that attenuates advocacy conversion even when authenticity and resonance perceptions are strong.

latest.title: Why Does Gamification Fail? The Impact Mechanisms of Gamification Design Flaws on Consumers' Continuous Purchase Intention
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Although e‐commerce platforms widely implement gamification designs, the potential negative effects on consumers and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To address this gap, this study employs a two‐stage mixed‐methods approach to uncover the influence mechanisms of gamification design flaws. In Study 1, we collected 24,749 consumer comments describing negative experiences with gamified shopping festivals. By combining BERTopic modeling with a human‐LLM collaboration, we identified seven latent concepts. Further analysis grounded in psychological reactance theory and affective events theory indicated that four gamification design flaws, namely narrative rhythm disruption, game interaction complexity, reward value distortion, and gameplay replaceability, affect consumers' continuous purchase intention through perceived manipulation and frustration. In Study 2, we collected survey responses from 398 consumers who participated in the gamified shopping festivals and used PLS‐SEM to test the proposed hypotheses. This research deepens understanding of the adverse side of gamification, contributes to theoretical perspectives on the mechanisms of gamification design flaws, and provides novel insights for optimizing gamification in e‐commerce platforms.

latest.title: Religiosity and consumer behaviour among Millennials and Gen Z: does gender make a difference?
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how religiosity is associated with consumer behaviour among Millennials and Gen Z in a highly religious emerging market. It proposes the spiritual cognitive consumption theory (SCCT), a dual pathway framework, and provides preliminary empirical support for its overall predictive validity. However, these two pathways were not directly measured; future experimental research is needed to isolate each mechanism. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 400 Nigerian respondents were analysed using structural equation modelling. Gender significantly moderates this relationship: women tend to show a stronger association between religiosity and relational aspects (e.g. brand trust, emotional congruity), whereas men focus more on instrumental outcomes (e.g. product functionality, religious symbolism). Findings The SCCT framework provides a nuanced understanding of the tension between spiritual devotion and market-based consumption. The findings offer marketers gender-sensitive, faith-conscious strategies and position SCCT as a robust theoretical tool for understanding spirituality, cognition and consumption in evolving digital economies. Social implications The study contributes to sustainable development goal (SDG) 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) by providing insights into inclusive, faith-sensitive marketing practices in the Global South. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in the development of the SCCT framework, which integrates spirituality, cognition and consumption into a dual pathway model. This offers a novel theoretical lens for understanding consumer behaviour in religious emerging markets.

latest.title: Parasocial relationships in informal digital beauty education: explainable machine learning evidence from YouTube beauty influencers
latest.venue: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
latest.abstract: Social media beauty influencers increasingly function as informal sources of procedural, product, and aesthetic knowledge, yet the relational mechanisms connecting audiences to these digital sources remain underexplored. This study examines parasocial relationship (PSR) strength in the Beauty & Fashion subset of a multimodal YouTube influencer dataset and introduces RAPID-PSR, a relational-aware, pseudo-labeled, interpretable ordinal ensemble framework. The dataset comprised 3,329 observations, including 819 usable human-annotated cases categorized as absent, weak, moderate, or strong PSR, and 2,483 application observations. RAPID-PSR combines behavioral and creator-context variables, engineered relational features, TF-IDF-based text representations, cumulative ordinal learning, an adaptive XGBoost-LightGBM-CatBoost ensemble, confidence-based pseudo-labeling, and ordinal SHAP explanations. An independent test partition (n = 158) was retained for evaluation. RAPID-PSR achieved 66.46% accuracy, macro-F1 = 0.553, quadratic weighted kappa = 0.647, ordinal MAE = 0.380, macro ROC-AUC = 0.810, and macro PR-AUC = 0.590. It produced the highest accuracy, macro-F1, QWK, and lowest ordinal error, while CatBoost achieved the strongest ROC-AUC and log-loss performance. SHAP analysis identified textual semantics, interaction depth, reciprocal engagement, interaction regularity, relational warmth, and sentiment as major predictors of PSR strength. Survey-linked validation further showed substantial convergence between computational and self-reported PSR scores (Pearson r = 0.666; Spearman ρ = 0.644). The findings highlight relational continuity and responsive interaction as important signals in creator-led informal beauty learning while emphasizing the distinction between interpersona

latest.title: Digital and social media marketing: a bibliometric mapping from 2020 to 2025
latest.abstract: Abstract Digital and social media marketing is reshaping how firms communicate with consumers, gather market intelligence, manage customer journeys, and build brand relationships. This study followed the PRISMA framework to select relevant Scopus-indexed articles between 2020 and 2025 under the business, management, and accounting subject area, using the search terms “digital marketing” and “social media marketing” in titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search, conducted on 20 February 2026 and restricted to open-access, English-language, final-stage journal articles, yielded 1,054 articles. Performance analysis, citation analysis, author-keyword co-occurrence mapping, an average-publication-year overlay, co-citation analysis, and bibliographic coupling were conducted using VOSviewer. Findings reveal publication growth, particularly during 2024 and 2025. Indonesia was the leading country by publications, whereas the UK was the most influential country by citations. Additionally, the “Journal of Business Research” is the most influential, while “Cogent Business & Management” is the most productive journal; the most-cited document is “Setting the future of digital and social media marketing research: Perspectives and research propositions,” with 1,806 citations, produced by “International Journal of Information Management.” Four of the ten prominent authors published six papers each, including Saura, J.R., and Huertas-Garcia, R., both affiliated with Spanish institutions. Keyword mapping identifies digital marketing, social media marketing, social media, consumer behavior, marketing, and purchase intention as central themes. This study clarifies the post-2020 knowledge structure of the open-access segment of this literature, proposes that digital and social media marketi

latest.title: From others to the self: Influence mechanisms of multiple social agents on sustainable consumption
latest.abstract: 摘要： 可持续消费研究长期聚焦个体消费者的心理与行为机制, 无力弥合可持续态度与实际消费行为之间的显著差距。理论演进的脉络梳理表明, 可持续消费的个体选择会受到消费者社会关系网络中多元社会主体的复杂影响。本文系统梳理个体、群体和组织层面的社会主体对消费者可持续消费的影响, 并基于自我决定理论提出了以基本心理需求和动机内化连续体为核心的社会主体影响机制与效应框架。未来研究应重点探讨如何完善多元主体对个体可持续消费的影响机制框架、拓展社会主体的研究边界、推动可持续消费的集体行动研究转向, 从而为破解可持续消费知易行难的现实困境拓展理论空间与实践路径。

latest.title: Experiential branding in the digital age: evaluative and experiential pathways from brand experience to customer satisfaction
latest.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study examines the psychological mechanisms linking brand experience and customer satisfaction. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S-O-R) framework and appraisal theory, it investigates the mediating roles of brand authenticity and brand engagement, treated, respectively, as an evaluative (cognitive-appraisal) and a multidimensional experiential-investment organismic pathway. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 304 smartphone consumers in Haryana NCR (India) using a structured questionnaire and a non-probability convenience sample. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM, SmartPLS 4) was used to test the model, which incorporates two reflective higher-order constructs and two mediators modelled in parallel (a formative Mode B re-estimation of the higher-order constructs, a sensitivity analysis with and without one affection item and a bootstrap contrast of the two specific indirect effects were added as robustness checks and a formal comparison). One indicator (AFFBENG3; loading 0.376) was removed post hoc; the structural results are the same when it is retained. Findings Brand experience is positively related to customer satisfaction, brand authenticity and brand engagement. Brand engagement ( β = 0.424) and brand authenticity ( β = 0.128) are both positively related to satisfaction, with engagement showing the numerically larger coefficient. Both specific indirect effects are significant (through engagement β = 0.107; through authenticity β = 0.048) alongside a significant direct path (β = 0.136), a pattern consistent with complementary partial mediation through two mediators modelled in parallel; because the direct path is small, this classification is treated cautiously. A bootstrap contrast showed

latest.title: AI-Enabled Hospitality Services and Consumer Repurchase Intention: The Roles of Technology Readiness, Technological Empowerment, Emotional Attachment, and Trust
latest.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
latest.abstract: This study investigates how technology adoption propensity (TAP) is associated with consumers’ intention to repurchase AI-enabled hospitality services by examining the mediating roles of perceived technological empowerment (PTE) and brand emotional attachment (BEA), as well as the moderating role of trust in AI (TAI). Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework and the technology readiness perspective, cross-sectional survey data were collected from 439 guests of deluxe hotels in Greater Cairo, Egypt, and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that TAP is positively associated with both PTE and BEA. PTE is positively associated with BEA and partially mediates the TAP–BEA association, and the sequential indirect association between TAP and repurchase intention through PTE and BEA is significant. BEA emerges as a strong predictor of repurchase intention, while TAI strengthens the relationship between BEA and repurchase intention. The study contributes by showing that a general technology predisposition is linked to post-adoption repurchase intentions through a cognitive-to-affective chain (empowerment, then brand attachment) while retaining a larger direct link to attachment, and by identifying trust in AI as a boundary condition of the attachment–intention link. Because the design is cross-sectional and measures intentions, the results indicate associations rather than causal effects.

latest.title: THE INFLUENCE OF DIGITAL MARKETING ON CONSUMER PURCHASING DECISIONS.
authors: Caroline Dias da Silva de Carvalho
latest.abstract: This article aimed to analyze the impact of digital marketing and digital influencers on consumer behavior. The methodology used comprised the following research methods: in the first phase, a bibliographic review was conducted in order to analyze, in the scientific literature, the transformation from traditional marketing to digital marketing, as well as the role of social media and digital influencers in purchase decisions; in the second stage, a field research was carried out through the application of a structured questionnaire, aiming to identify consumers' perceptions regarding the influence exerted by these agents on their consumption habits. The results obtained indicated that digital marketing significantly influenced consumer behavior, making consumers more active and informed, while digital influencers exerted a strong impact on opinion formation and purchase decisions, especially due to the credibility and identification established with the audience. It was concluded that digital marketing and digital influencers played an essential role in contemporary business strategies, being fundamental for building relationships with consumers and strengthening brands in the digital environment.

latest.title: Identificação da utilização do método hipotético-dedutivo nos estudos de Destination Branding na base de dados Hospitality & Tourism Complete – EBSCOhost
latest.venue: RELACult - Revista Latino-Americana de Estudos em Cultura e Sociedade
latest.abstract: A teoria do destination branding tem sido amplamente utilizada para investigar marcas de destinos turísticos, consolidados ou emergentes. Sua natureza abrangente permite avaliar constructos essenciais para compreender a representação do destino e sua competitividade no mercado. A marca, ao comunicar atributos culturais, sociais e experienciais, torna-se um instrumento estratégico na diferenciação territorial e no fortalecimento da atratividade turística. Este estudo tem como objetivo identificar o uso do método hipotético-dedutivo em artigos alinhados à perspectiva neopositivista, disponíveis na base Hospitality & Tourism Complete – EBSCOhost. Adotou-se uma abordagem qualitativa, de caráter exploratório, utilizando o levantamento bibliométrico. A busca inicial resultou na identificação de 232 artigos por meio das palavras-chave “destination”, “branding” e “management”. A triagem realizada no software Excel permitiu selecionar os estudos que abordavam especificamente o destination branding, resultando em 54 artigos, dos quais 14 empregavam o método hipotético-dedutivo. Os resultados evidenciam que o destination branding desempenha papel relevante na construção da imagem de destino e na consolidação de estratégias de marketing territorial. As tendências de pesquisa observadas reforçam a importância de modelos teóricos que permitam mensurar variáveis relacionadas à marca, contribuindo para avanços teóricos e práticos. Nos estudos analisados, as abordagens neopositivistas sustentadas pelo método hipotético-dedutivo demonstram potencial para aprimorar a gestão turística, uma vez que permitem testar hipóteses, identificar relações causais e fortalecer a compreensão dos constructos que influenciam o desempenho das marcas destino. Observa-se que o destination branding permanece

latest.title: The influence of AI chatbots’ human-like and technical characteristics on users’ perceived addictiveness
latest.abstract: With the widespread adoption of generative AI chatbots, their human-like and technical characteristics may enhance user experience while also increasing the risks of overdependence and potential addiction. However, how these two categories of characteristics jointly shape users’ perceived addictiveness remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework, this study developed a model integrating perceived empathy, social presence, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, trust, emotional attachment, functional dependence, and perceived addictiveness. Data were collected from 345 Chinese AI chatbot users through an online survey and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results showed that perceived empathy, social presence, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use all positively influenced trust, which in turn strengthened emotional attachment and functional dependence. Both emotional attachment and functional dependence increased perceived addictiveness, with emotional attachment exerting the stronger effect. Mediation analysis further indicated that chatbot characteristics indirectly influenced perceived addictiveness through two parallel pathways: trust–emotional attachment and trust–functional dependence. These findings reveal the emotional and functional mechanisms underlying perceived AI chatbot addictiveness, extend the S–O–R framework, and provide implications for responsible design, calibrated trust, and dependence-risk governance.

latest.title: Authenticity in marketing: A conceptual model and meta-analysis
latest.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
latest.abstract: Abstract Authenticity drives customer decision-making and firm success, yet research remains fragmented due to the diversity of conceptualizations, mediators and outcomes, and empirical contexts investigated. Utilizing the entity–referent correspondence framework, we distinguish true-to-fact, true-to-ideal, and true-to-self authenticity as antecedents of overall perceived authenticity. This conceptualization of authenticity types applies to a range of entities including brands, experiences, individuals, places, and products. Our meta-analysis, utilizing 406 independent samples and 173,577 customers, demonstrates that the most integrative model (comprising the three authenticity types and overall authenticity) performs best. It uncovers causal chains linking authenticity to mediators (positive affect, positive beliefs, relationship quality) and outcomes (satisfaction, word-of-mouth, repurchase intentions). To evaluate generalizability, we include offer-related (hedonic vs. utilitarian, durable vs. consumable, services vs. goods, human vs. non-human), market-related (online vs. offline, high vs. low coproduction), and country-specific (emerging vs. developed markets, individualism vs. collectivism) moderators. The results offer managerial guidance for aligning offerings with customer expectations.

latest.title: Unveiling the role of virtual streamer’s interaction attributes in shaping consumer-generated value behaviors
latest.abstract: The interaction attributes of virtual streamers are crucial to their success. This study deconstructs virtual streamers' interaction into two dimensions: interaction intelligence and interaction humanness. Drawing on immersion theory and parasocial relationship theory, the study examines how these interaction attributes are associated with consumer-generated value behaviors, including social media engagement, donation, and purchase intention. Using data from a survey of 479 respondents and structural equation modeling, the results reveal that both the interaction intelligence and interaction humanness of virtual streamers are positively associated with consumer immersion, which, in turn, is positively related to parasocial relationships with virtual streamers. Immersion and parasocial relationships are further associated with social media engagement, donation, and purchase intention. This study advances the theoretical understanding of virtual streamer interaction and provides practical insights for content creators and platforms aiming to foster consumer-generated value behaviors in virtual streaming.

latest.title: AFETO PARA UNS, PRATICIDADE PARA OUTROS: A PARTICIPAÇÃO DOS ASPECTOS AFETIVOS NA ESCOLHA DE INSTITUIÇÕES FINANCEIRAS
latest.abstract: Com a digitalização dos serviços financeiros, bancos tradicionais, cooperativas de crédito e fintechs ficaram mais parecidos, e aspectos afetivos ganharam espaço na escolha do consumidor. Este estudo analisou de que forma esses aspectos participam da escolha de instituições financeiras e se essa participação é semelhante entre os consumidores. Foi realizado um survey com 291 consumidores de Foz do Iguaçu-PR, que avaliaram oito afirmações em escala Likert de cinco pontos, analisadas por estatística descritiva, tabulação cruzada e teste qui-quadrado. O afeto apareceu no momento da escolha, pela experiência pessoal e pelo sentimento em relação à instituição, e na relação com ela, pelo vínculo, pela disposição para defendê-la e pelo sentimento de ser valorizado. A praticidade se comportou como critério oposto ao afeto, pois quem a priorizou se afastou das afirmações afetivas. Conclui-se que o afeto participa da decisão, mas não da mesma forma para todos, o que sugere perfis distintos de consumidores.

latest.title: Entrepreneurial Drivers and Performance in Indonesia’s Creative Sector
latest.abstract: The creative industry stands out as a key sector with strong potential to foster sustainable national economic development by generating employment, boosting exports, and strengthening cultural identity. Nevertheless, it encounters considerable obstacles, especially in relation to entrepreneurial capabilities, which are often hindered by limited education, insufficient experience, and restricted access to resources and business networks. The frequent incidence of the "valley of death" during the early phases of business formation underscores the critical need for robust and adaptable entrepreneurial competency development. This research explores the key factors that shape entrepreneurial competence and examines their influence on building sustainable business performance in West Java's creative industries. It focuses on assessing the roles of knowledge, skills, entrepreneurial orientation, social capital, and entrepreneurial personality in shaping entrepreneurial competence, and how these competencies, in turn, impact various dimensions of business performance. A total of 259 creative entrepreneurs, each with a minimum of 3.5 years of business experience, participated in the study. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results indicate that knowledge, skills, entrepreneurial orientation, and social capital significantly contribute to the development of entrepreneurial competence, whereas entrepreneurial personality does not present a meaningful effect. Moreover, enhanced entrepreneurial competence is shown to positively affect business outcomes such as sales growth, profit margins, customer satisfaction, and loyalty. latest.title: Mapping headphone brand positioning from e-commerce reviews with large language models
latest.abstract: Online consumer reviews encode rich signals about brands, yet converting this unstructured text into actionable positioning insight remains challenging. This study proposes an LLM-driven framework that extracts structured brand perception variables from e-commerce reviews and demonstrates it in the headphone category. Using an analytic file of 5,895 review-level observations covering Sony, Bose, JBL, and Beats, we employ a structured GPT-5.4 prompt to extract multidimensional brand perception indicators from each review, capturing associations, judgments, emotional attachment, advocacy, and attribute focus. A manual validation exercise based on 400 stratified reviews showed meaningful agreement between the LLM-coded outputs and an adjudicated human benchmark. The results reveal clear brand separation. Bose leads on perceived quality (4.20/5), recommendation rate (78.3%), and strong emotional connection (39.9%), whereas Sony achieves the highest value perception (3.97/5). Beats and JBL occupy weaker quality positions, though Beats retains a comparatively stronger emotional profile. Patterns in attribute emphasis also help distinguish the brands: Bose reviews are distributed across sound quality, active noise cancellation, and comfort; Sony reviews emphasize sound quality, comfort, and value; JBL reviews are heavily concentrated around sound quality; and Beats reviews emphasize sound quality, value, and design. Negative reviews provide additional diagnostic insight, revealing durability and fit issues for JBL and perceived value concerns for Beats. The study contributes primarily to LLM-assisted marketing analytics and applied brand diagnosis by showing how constrained and human-validated LLM coding can transform review text into a scalable, multidimensional brand monitor

latest.title: Structural insights into the effects of generative AI-empowered social media marketing on customer-brand engagement and purchase behaviors: evidence from China's platform economy
latest.abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities in enhancing customer purchase intentions through the mediating roles of brand equity and relationship equity within China’s platform economy. As generative artificial intelligence increasingly transforms digital interactions between brands and consumers, understanding its influence on customer engagement and purchasing behavior has become increasingly important. Data were collected from 620 Chinese consumers and analyzed using structural equation modeling to examine the relationships among generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities, customer–brand engagement, brand equity, relationship equity, and purchase intention. The findings reveal that generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities exert significant positive effects on customer–brand engagement, purchase intention, brand equity, and relationship equity. Brand equity significantly enhances both customer–brand engagement and purchase intention, confirming its important role in converting artificial intelligence-enabled social media marketing efforts into favorable consumer outcomes. Relationship equity significantly influences purchase intention but does not significantly affect customer–brand engagement. Furthermore, customer–brand engagement does not significantly influence purchase intention. The mediation results indicate that brand equity significantly mediates the effects of generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities on both customer–brand engagement and purchase intention.
